findings.evidence:

rulings.item: AQ-V4-05: cumulative reading of the V2.2 PA-1.4 rows (BA-02b V4 section 3)
rulings.recommendation:
RULING: accept the cumulative reading as the Architect's reading of PA-1.4, recorded like AR3-19, with three precisions.
(1) Cell precedence. Where a PA-1.4 cell contradicts a V2.1 31 cell of the same control, the PA-1.x text governs. The only such cells are the Class cells of LIBRARY_FRESHNESS and CLONE_POLICY_VERIFIED (UNRESOLVED in V2.1), which PA-1.1 and PA-1.2 make B and A. The GROUP column of section 31 is never the group authority: AFFECTED_GROUPS come from PA-1.2 and the groups from PA-1.3.
(2) Union. For SCENARIO CLASSES and MINIMUM CATALOG REQUIREMENT, the clauses of the V2.1 row and of the PA-1.4 row of the same control both apply. The PA-1.4 E-12 row (phase A, determinism, phase C, phase D) applies in addition to V2.1 rows R12 and R13, to all four controls E12A, E12DET, E12C and E12D. 'Subscription' in R13 is phase D (PA-1.2 naming).
(3) S-5 components. The PA-1.4 rows for the S-5 components (P1, P2) are added rows. V2.1 row R03 (S-5, groups AB, PR-REC, PW) also covered what PA-1.1 ratifies as derivations of S-5, so under the same reading it also names S5REC, S5MAN and S5CLO. This changes no state.
No BA-02b V4 state changes under either reading.
rulings.reasoning:
- V2.2 0.2 classifies section 31 as 'amended', not replaced; only 30 and 21.4 are replaced.
- The precedence rule of V2.2 0.1 ('for every clause named in this document, V2.2 governs over V2.1; every other clause of V2.1 stands unchanged') gives V2.2 priority only where the texts conflict.
- PA-1.4 says 'replaced or added rows' but never pairs a row with the V2.1 row it replaces. Its E-12 row spans two V2.1 rows, so any replacement reading would need an invented mapping.
- The union is the fail-closed reading. V2.1 1.6 requires a complete matrix for TRUE, and PA-1.5 repeats this.
- The union imposes no new obligation: every V2.1 clause it keeps is independently required elsewhere in the contract. Examples: warm-up loads outside the manifest refuse the run (V2.1 13.1 row 3, line 718), and validation plans lie structurally outside the learning corpus (V2.1 27.2 step 6 and 27.8, lines 1440-1444).
- A replacement reading would drop only R11 'a warm-up load outside the manifest refuses the run', R12, R13 and R16 'SOURCE_SWAP_CONTROL' as requirements. Every P row that would remain is discharged in BA-02b V4, so no state depends on the choice.
- The ruling does not block candidate readiness beyond fixing the normative text of BA-02b section 3. It is listed among BA-04's before-candidate prerequisites (BA-11 V4 line 119), and BA-02b inherits it through DEPENDS_ON.

rulings.item: R-3: AR3-03 for controls with several conditional negative controls, and the consequence of NEGATIVE_CONTROL_NOT_EVALUATED (BA02V4-N02)
rulings.recommendation:
Rule four points:
(a) The BA-02b rule 5 reading 'NEGATIVE_CONTROL_NOT_EVALUATED unless at least one of its conditional negative controls resolved to its detection branch' is accepted per control. It matches V2.1 31 check 2 ('at least one ... deliberate-violation scenario'), and AR3-03's 'su celda' is per scenario.
(b) At acceptance, NEGATIVE_CONTROL_NOT_EVALUATED makes V2.1 31 check 2 NOT MET for that control.
(c) V2.1 1.6 'the coverage matrix (section 31) is complete' is read as checks 1 to 4 all met. A control in NEGATIVE_CONTROL_NOT_EVALUATED therefore keeps ALT21D_HOST_PASS at NOT_EVALUATED and never TRUE.
(d) The group verdict of a conditional negative control is 'designed detection' only on its detection branch.
rulings.reasoning:
- AR3-03 fixes the BA-02b state ('nunca MET ni PASS') but not what that state does to the predicate.
- As V4 is written, check 4 (the only incompleteness test of V2.1 31) stays PASS, so an E-12 phase C or S-5 negative control that is never evaluated would not prevent TRUE. That defeats the fail-closed purpose of AR2-12, AR3-03 and AR3-04.
- For E12C the choice matters: there are 19 conditional negative controls, and NC-E12C (Wr-A at X6 under CER-WIT) duplicates the stimulus of WR-A-X6.

If AQ-V4-03 makes the KS-* scenarios serve KS through a control, the contract-assigned entries become unnecessary and must be removed so that they never duplicate GROUPS_SERVED.
rulings.reasoning:
- The PA-1.3 group KS covers 'Selective seams SL-1, SL-2, SL-4, SL-5, SL-6 (comparators S-1..S-3)', and V2.1 31 lists KS-* for SC-A and KS.
- Since BA04V3-09 the KS-* scenarios stop at PS, so they exercise none of S-1..S-3.
- Until the ruling, no PASS risk exists (the membership is evidence-only), but it extends a closed decision.

findings.location: md section 1.1; md section 4, tuple row CHARACTERIZATION_TUPLE; JSON TUPLE_REQUIREMENTS of the 316 CHARACTERIZATION_BUILD scenarios; BUILD_UNDER_TEST of Q-I01..Q-I16, Q-I09-LOSS, Q-I10-LOSS, Q-SIGNED-ZERO, Q-FPSPEC-VECTORS, Q-ROUTE-R1, Q-I16-CLEANUP-NEG, E6-C1..E6-C8 and Q-I14; md section 8 AQ-V4-06
findings.claim: The characterization-build tuple keeps every other BUILD_BOUND field equal to the product baseline. For the fields that depend on the build (the Plugin and harness DLL hashes, the manifest build layer that E-10 and WARMUP_MEMBERSHIP compare with exact equality, and the instrument qualification records of the exact build) this cannot hold. Every characterization-build run, including the AR3-01 pin-source runs and all 161 WU-DRY, would therefore be refused at P0 or be INVALID. No instrument is qualified on the characterization build, and Q-I14 is declared on a build where I-14 does not exist.
findings.evidence: md 4: 'CHARACTERIZATION_TUPLE: FULL_BASELINE_TUPLE in which the build under test is the baseline CHARACTERIZATION_BUILD (its build receipt and DLL SHA-256 are BUILD_BOUND fields ...); every other field as in FULL_BASELINE_TUPLE'. md 1.1 says the build differs 'by those switches and their declared harness assemblies', and 'Every other control stays fail-closed (V2.1 3.2)', which covers E-10 and WUM. V2.1 2.1 BUILD_BOUND fields include 'Plugin DLL SHA-256', 'manifest version and hash (build layer)' and 'instrument qualification records for the exact build (section 4.3)'. V2.1 12.3, baseline row: 'two snapshots equal each other and equal the manifest set entry by entry (path and hash); no other member' => refuse (O1), 'EXACT set equality'. V2.1 13.1 step 3: 'a warm-up load outside the manifest refuses the run'. V2.1 4.3: 'Every instrument I-01..I-16 must be qualified on the exact execution build before any governing run ... a governing run with an unqualified instrument cannot yield a PASS'; row I-14: 'usable only in characterization builds'. JSON: 316 scenarios use CHARACTERIZATION_BUILD (125 governing outside the mode, 191 in the mode). Every Q-I*, Q-SIGNED-ZERO, Q-FPSPEC-VECTORS, Q-ROUTE-R1, Q-I16-CLEANUP-NEG and E6-C* is PRODUCT_BUILD. Q-I14 is PRODUCT_BUILD, yet its EXPECTED_PROCEDURAL_RESULT ends 'usable only in characterization builds', and the Q-I14-X NOTE says 'the I-14 writers exist only there, V2.1 4.3 row I-14'. The characterization-build governing scenarios still declare 'every instrument RELIABLE (qualified on the exact build)'. md 8 AQ-V4-06 raises 'two build identities' but not the manifest or qualification consequences.
findings.required_fix: Under the AQ-V4-06 ruling: (1) Define CHARACTERIZATION_TUPLE with its own values for every build-dependent BUILD_BOUND field: the Plugin and harness DLL SHA-256, the manifest build layer and hash (the E-10 known set and the WUM membership set of that build), the warm-up definition if it differs, and the instrument qualification records of that build. (2) Add the qualification scenarios I-01..I-16 on the CHARACTERIZATION_BUILD, or obtain a sealed Architect ruling that a named subset transfers. (3) Move Q-I14 to CHARACTERIZATION_BUILD. (4) State how the claim that the build differs 'only by the switches' is verified and recorded. Pins derived on it (E04, LOCK_MODE, HOST_DEFAULT_MAP) are applied to 65 PRODUCT_BUILD governing runs. (5) Align BA-07 (per-build manifest), BA-08 K-10, BA-09 W-7 and BA-11.

findings.location: NC-E12A: EXPECTED_PRODUCT_OUTCOME, EXPECTED_CONTROL_RESULTS.E12A, CONDITIONAL_EXPECTATION_RULE
findings.claim: The only E-12 phase-A negative control declares E12A FAIL and the abort unconditionally. The detection needs the injected XData event to be delivered, and on the non-delivery branch the run commits. The declared result then has no authority, and a missed delivery would be charged to E12-V as a class-B FAIL instead of leaving the cell uncovered.
findings.evidence: NC-E12A: E12A 'FAIL (unattributable event)', outcome 'O2 (CER-ABV)', CONDITIONAL_EXPECTATION_RULE 'CER-ABV'. S1 and E08 are PASS by design ('outside the fingerprinted fields', 'not in the read-set'), so the only abort cause is a delivered phase-A event. V2.1 14, phase table: 'inference | absence of events is not a signal'. V2.1 14.1: which events fire 'is a characterization result'. AR2-12: 'toda regla condicional que dependa de "evento entregado" se resuelve con el registro del testigo de entrega del I-14'. The phase-C analogue NC-E12C uses CER-WIT, with 'NOT_RUNNABLE for NC-E12C when not delivered'. V2.1 31 check 2 needs a deliberate violation per control, and BA-02b counts NC-E12A as the E12A violation cell.
findings.required_fix: Make NC-E12A conditional through CER-WIT. On delivery: E12A FAIL, abort before Commit(), then O2/O6 by CER-ABV. On non-delivery: NOT_RUNNABLE for NC-E12A, E12A PASS, the run commits (O3), and the cell is NEGATIVE_CONTROL_NOT_EVALUATED (AR3-03). This requires the witness to be qualified for XDATA_WRITE at Y1 (BA04V4-05). Recompute SEALED_AT and the BA-02b E12A row.

findings.location: WU-DRY-NC-E12A, WU-DRY-NC-E04-R2, WU-DRY-NC-E03-NOT-HELD, WU-DRY-NC-E03-REACQUIRE, WU-DRY-NC-S1-Y1, WU-DRY-NC-S1-Y1-SILENT (REACH, EXPECTED_LOG_RECORD_SET, EXPECTED_EVENTS, STATUS, BLOCKED_BY); md section 5.2 'Branches the dry runs do not take'
findings.claim: These six dry runs keep the truncated REACH, log profile and events of their source, while md 5.2 and BA-09 V4 section 4 say they do not take the refusal or abort branch and keep running. In one case (a suppressed lock) continuing means writing without the document lock. They are SEALED_PENDING_PIN_CANDIDATE although their plan depends on the open AQ-V4-02.
findings.evidence: md 5.2: 'the dry run records that failure and does not take the branch (it keeps running where X would stop)'. BA-09 V4 section 4: 'the run reaches PV, Commit(), V1 and PC wherever the path of X does'. JSON: WU-DRY-NC-E04-R2 REACH P0 with 'LP-DRY over LP-P0'. WU-DRY-NC-E03-NOT-HELD REACH PL with 'LP-DRY over LP-PL'. WU-DRY-NC-E12A, -NC-E03-REACQUIRE, -NC-S1-Y1 and -NC-S1-Y1-SILENT have REACH PV with 'LP-DRY over LP-PV', and EXPECTED_EVENTS lists only PREPARE (0) and MUTATION (A). LP-PV contains 'ABORT x1; ABORT_VERIFY x1' and LP-P0 contains 'OUTCOME x1'. NC-E03-NOT-HELD suppresses the lock acquisition, and V2.1 8 has the orchestrator hold LockDocument from PL through V1, so continuing past PL means PREPARE-W and T_M writes with no lock, a path the contract does not define. The six have STATUS SEALED_PENDING_PIN_CANDIDATE and BLOCKED_BY [], while md 8 lists AQ-V4-02 as open.
findings.required_fix: After the AQ-V4-02 ruling, choose one of two options. (a) A characterization-build switch takes the declared branch at the same checkpoint: keep REACH and the profile, and name the switch in PLAN_OR_INPUT and INJECTIONS. (b) Declare the path actually traversed: REACH CP, 'LP-DRY over LP-CP', and phases B, C and POST_V1_TO_CP in EXPECTED_EVENTS. For NC-E03-NOT-HELD only (a) is sound. Until the ruling, mark the six DRAFT and BLOCKED_BY AQ-V4-02, and add AQ-V4-02 to the vocabulary.

findings.location: md section 4 log profiles LP-PS, LP-PV and LP-CP (JSON LOG_PROFILES); EXPECTED_LOG_RECORD_SET and EXPECTED_EVIDENCE_SET of the 83 scenarios whose CONDITIONAL_EXPECTATION_RULE uses CER-WIT, CER-SIL, CER-PERSIST or CER-A2, and of the 141 governing injected scenarios
findings.claim: The conditional rules resolve from sealed I-14 records of the same run: the delivery witness and the independent post-abort read. No profile or evidence set of the governing scenarios declares these records, and no profile declares an injection record. The declared log is incomplete for 83 conditional scenarios, and by the catalog's own rule an unresolvable conditional becomes UNKNOWN.
findings.evidence: CER-WIT: 'resolved offline from the sealed I-14 DELIVERY WITNESS record of the same run'. CER-PERSIST: 'from the sealed I-14 independent post-abort read'. CER-A2: 'from the sealed I-14 delivery witness record of the same run only'. LP-CP, LP-PV and LP-PS contain E12_EVENT but no WITNESS, INJECTION or POST_ABORT_READ record. Only LP-CHAR has 'WRITER_EFFECT x1 and WITNESS x1 per injection (Q-I14-*)'. EXPECTED_EVIDENCE_SET = EVIDENCE_PACKAGE_STANDARD (V2.1 18.2, whose events are only 'E-11M and E-12 logs'). V2.1 26.1: 'the record types and counts the run log must contain'. md 3: 'a rule that the sealed evidence cannot resolve makes the scenario result UNKNOWN'.
findings.required_fix: Add to LP-PS, LP-PV and LP-CP (or as per-scenario deltas): INJECTION x1 per injection, WITNESS x1 per injection position for the CER-WIT and CER-A2 scenarios, and POST_ABORT_READ x1 for NC-S5-O6. Also name the I-14 witness log in the evidence set of these scenarios.

findings.location: md section 1.2 writer kinds Wr-OCT and XDATA_WRITE; Q-I14-Y and Q-I14-X INJECTIONS and PLAN_OR_INPUT; NC-S5-O6 (CER-PERSIST); NC-E12A

Neither does the 'I-14 independent post-abort read' that CER-PERSIST resolves from. The coordinate qualifications cover only Wr-A..Wr-G.
findings.evidence: md 1.2 lists 'Wr-OCT | a write through an OpenCloseTransaction at a Y position (NC-S5-O6, AR3-04) (build switch)' and 'XDATA_WRITE | ... through T_M at a Y position (NC-E12A) (build switch)'. Q-I14-Y INJECTIONS: [{writer 'Wr-A..Wr-G', position 'Y0, Y1 and Y2'}]. Q-I14-X: Wr-A..Wr-G at X0..X8. The base Q-I14 has no fixture and no coordinate. V2.1 4.3 row I-14: 'each writer produces its intended modification and events (verified by an independent read)'. V2.1 4.3: an unqualified instrument cannot support a PASS. findings.location: NC-CLONE-REPLACE: PLAN_OR_INPUT, INJECTIONS, EXPECTED_DETECTION_CHANNEL
findings.claim: The scenario forces DuplicateRecordCloning.Replace but does not say what the importer declares. The contract lets PREPARE-W start only when the declared mode is on the allow-list. If the switch also changes the declaration, the run is refused before any import (O1), not the O6 ruled by AR3-07.
findings.evidence: PLAN: 'a switch of the characterization build forces DuplicateRecordCloning.Replace for the SL-5 import (a cloning mode outside the allow-list)'. V2.1 7.1: 'The importer must declare the mode it used ... and PREPARE-W does not start unless the declared mode is on the allow-list'. BA-06 V4 CQ-02 reading: 'the importer declares its cloning mode before the first import ... PREPARE-W starts only if the declaration is on the allow-list, and a result that declares another mode is the cloning FAIL'. Code at 3375aadb (BlockLibraryImporter.cs:123) hard-codes Ignore, with no declaration. AR3-07 fixes the path: import, effect check, CLONE FAIL, stop at PREPARE-W, O6.
findings.required_fix: State in PLAN_OR_INPUT and INJECTIONS that the switch forces the effective mode while the importer's pre-import declaration stays on the allow-list. State whether the structured result re-declares Replace, and if so name that as the first CLONE detection channel, next to the effect check. Keep this consistent with the AQ-V4-11 (CQ-02) ruling.

findings.location: PW-CLONE-WRONG-TYPE: EXPECTED_PROCEDURAL_RESULT and EXPECTED_CONTROL_RESULTS.S5CLO
findings.claim: The procedural expectation describes an import that never happens in this scenario, and the S5CLO expectation is not a control result.
findings.evidence: REACH 'PR', outcome 'O1', CLONE 'PASS: the wrong-type homonym is REJECTED before any write ... nothing written', LP-PR. Yet EXPECTED_PROCEDURAL_RESULT reads 'the import or reuse executed under the declared cloning mode; exact fingerprints compared'. S5CLO: 'REJECT recorded (...) => PREPARE-R rejection'. V2.1 26.1: EXPECTED_CONTROL_RESULTS is 'per control: PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN'. V2.1 5, PR row: 'FAIL | any rejection decision'. V2.2 PA-3 compares EXPECTED_PROCEDURAL_RESULT.
findings.required_fix: Set EXPECTED_PROCEDURAL_RESULT to the refusal ('closure classified; REJECT recorded; refusal before PREPARE-W; nothing imported'). Give S5CLO an exact result (for example FAIL, the rejection decision of V2.1 5 PR row), or remove it and let the default apply with a stated reason. Recompute SEALED_AT.

findings.location: HDM-CHAR-FX1F, HDM-CHAR-FXANN, HDM-CHAR-FXDIM: PLAN_OR_INPUT, INJECTIONS, FIXTURE, PIN_SLOTS, REPETITION
findings.claim: The informative runs with a varied key are part of each scenario's repetition, but the changed input is not declared: no injection, no fixture variant and no pin slot. The scenario's declared input is therefore not the input of those runs.
findings.evidence: PLAN: '... and, outside the intent, at least one informative run per key variable with that key changed', with the keys CLAYER, CECOLOR, CELTYPE, CELTSCALE, CELWEIGHT, CETRANSPARENCY, CPLOTSTYLE and the current text and dimension style. REPETITION: 'CHAR_RUNS = N_A at the pinned key values, plus at least one informative run per varied key'. INJECTIONS []. PIN_SLOTS ['FIXTURE_INSTANCE@FX-1F','LOCK_MODE']. BA-08 V4 12 requires the keys to be equal in every template, so a changed key means either a template that is not the pinned instance or a control-plane change before P0. md 1.2 has CONTROL_PLANE_SETUP and FIXTURE_VARIANT kinds for exactly this. V2.1 26.1: FIXTURE 'by hash'; INJECTIONS 'writers ... or none'.
findings.required_fix: Declare the key change of the informative runs as a CONTROL_PLANE_SETUP injection before P0 (per key: the variable, the value set and the position), or as declared template variants with their own FIXTURE_INSTANCE slots. State that these runs carry no intent and are excluded from the pin record's lookup entries, except as dependence evidence (BA-08 V4 HDM-4, HDM-5).

findings.location: EA2-DEFERRED-EVENTS (CONTROLS_EXERCISED includes A1; EXPECTED_CONTROL_RESULTS lacks A1); CER-A2 (md section 3)
findings.claim: On the CER-A2 branches where a write event is delivered after V0, the default rule expects A-1 PASS in the same run. Nothing attributes a delivered W-scan event to A-2 rather than to the verifier's read-only opens (A-1).
findings.evidence: EA2 CONTROLS_EXERCISED includes 'A1' and 'A2', and EXPECTED_CONTROL_RESULTS has only A2 and E12C. So by UNLISTED_CONTROLS A1 is expected PASS, including when 'a deferred event delivered between V0 and V1 => O7, A-2 FAIL'. V2.1 14, phase table: 'no origin inference'. V2.1 14.7 defines A-1 by the EA1 experiment (read-only opens alone) and A-2 by known-correct commits. In a mirror run, W-scan contains both the verifier's read-only opens and any deferred commit events.
findings.required_fix: State how A-1 is evaluated in a mirror run. Either remove A1 from EA2's (and the clean runs') CONTROLS_EXERCISED, leaving A-1 to EA1, or declare A1 conditional in CER-A2: an event delivered in W-scan cannot be attributed, so A-1 and A-2 are both recorded as not PASS (UNKNOWN), or the rule names the authority that attributes it. Recompute SEALED_AT and GROUPS_SERVED.

findings.location: md section 1.3 field list; JSON SEALED_AT_RULE.fields
findings.claim: SEALED_AT leaves out the fields that say which groups a scenario's verdict is counted for (GROUP, EVIDENCE_GROUPS_DECLARED, CONTRACT_ASSIGNED_GROUPS). Changing them changes neither SEALED_AT nor SCENARIO_VERSION, although the hashed EXPECTED_GROUP_VERDICT depends on them.
findings.evidence: SEALED_AT_RULE.fields has 30 fields; GROUP, EVIDENCE_GROUPS_DECLARED and CONTRACT_ASSIGNED_GROUPS are not among them. GROUPS_SERVED is derived from CONTROLS_EXERCISED (hashed) plus EVIDENCE_GROUPS_DECLARED (not hashed). EXPECTED_GROUP_VERDICT is hashed and refers to them, for example WR-A-X7: '... (contributes to the groups served); SC-B: tail-log or residual evidence only (CONTRACT_ASSIGNED_GROUPS; never PASS)'. V2.1 26.1: SCENARIO_VERSION changes on 'a change of any expectation'; EXPECTED_GROUP_VERDICT is 'the group verdict the scenario contributes'. AR3-25 leaves 'los campos de expectativa' to be defined.
findings.required_fix: Add GROUP, EVIDENCE_GROUPS_DECLARED and CONTRACT_ASSIGNED_GROUPS to the SEALED_AT field set and recompute all values, or state in md 1.3 why group membership is not an expectation and how its change is versioned.

findings.location: md header PREREQUISITES and DELTA RULING APPLIED; md 7.1 C-3; md 4 REPETITION_RULES.DEFAULT; REPETITION of 16 scenarios; md 2.1; JSON DELTA_RULING_APPLIED

rulings.item: AQ-V4-01: RECORDED_NOT_ENFORCED set and build of the governing learning runs EV-L-* and the qualification vehicles Q-I14-*, including BA-06 V4 CQ-08
rulings.recommendation: RULE, with a different answer for each part. (1) EV-L-*: stay GOVERNING for group E12-L (V2.2 PA-3). RECORDED_NOT_ENFORCED = {E-12 phase A, E-12 phase C} on the contract ground (V2.1 27.2 steps 2-5; V2.1 14.3 level 2 'frozen after learning'; V2.2 PA-2: only a FROZEN model is used by governing validation). E-03 is ENFORCED under the LOCK_MODE pin, which precedes learning (AR2-11 order, BA-04 V4 2.2 steps 3 to 6, LP-LEARN LOCK record). E-04 is recorded and not enforced, for a V2.1 3.3 reason rather than as an AR3-01 extension: the admitted set is defined per checkpoint (P0, PL, PV, PC) for the designated route of the mirror command, and a micro-scenario is neither. S-1..S-3 are NOT_EVALUATED, not RECORDED_NOT_ENFORCED (AR2-25: a micro-scenario builds no VERIFY_ELEMENT_LIST). Every other control stays fail-closed ('manifest-attested', 27.2 step 2). EXPECTED_PRODUCT_OUTCOME = NONE, since there is no mirror product run. (2) Build and CQ-08: yes, under V2.1 27.5 ('any change to ... the tuple ... requires a new model version, review and revalidation') the learning build identity is part of what the model is valid for. Learning (EV-L-*) and validation (EV-V-*, now on PRODUCT_BUILD) must share every BUILD_BOUND field that can affect events. Either run EV-L-* on the validation build, with the micro-scenario driver declared as a harness DLL (V2.1 2.1) that is present and inert in validation, or move EV-V-* to the same characterization build (then AQ-V4-06 applies). (3) Q-I14-*: accept the proposal. They are qualification vehicles (V2.1 4.3 row I-14, 'usable only in characterization builds'). The qualification verdict comes from the writer-effect and witness records against the independent read, so the vehicle's product result is not adjudicated, and the AR3-01 set may apply to the vehicle on the CHARACTERIZATION_BUILD. They stay governing Q evidence (AR2-22 precedent) and keep their WU-DRY under AR3-02. Extend them to Wr-OCT, XDATA_WRITE and the post-abort read (BA04V4-05). Blocks: 25 scenarios (C-3a), and the BA-06 V4 section 9 learning definition.
rulings.reasoning: AR3-01 rules the mode only for non-governing pre-EVM runs and does not change the phase policy of governing runs. For learning, the contract grounds only the E-12 A/C part: no EVM exists yet. The pins that exist before learning (LOCK_MODE) let E-03 be enforced, and V2.1 27.2 step 2 asks for a controlled environment. E-04 and S-1..S-3 are not applicable to a micro-scenario for structural reasons (3.3, AR2-25), not because of AR3-01. V2.1 27.5 and 27.1 make the model's validity depend on the tuple, so the learning and validation builds must be the same or be shown event-neutral. For Q-I14, V2.1 4.3 itself requires the characterization build, and what they qualify is independent of the product controls.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-02: dry-run branches whose source refusal comes from a RECORDED_NOT_ENFORCED control (NC-E12A, NC-E04-R2, NC-E03-NOT-HELD, NC-E03-REACQUIRE, NC-S1-Y1, NC-S1-Y1-SILENT)
rulings.recommendation: RULE: the dry run must take the source's declared branch at the same checkpoint through a characterization-build switch. The switch records the value of the RECORDED_NOT_ENFORCED control and then performs the refusal or abort that X declares. The AR3-01 mode stays: AR3-02, 'solo miden cargas', removes the dependency on the pins, not the path. With this ruling the six dry runs keep their declared REACH and profiles, and the switch must be named in PLAN_OR_INPUT and INJECTIONS (BA04V4-02). If the Architect prefers the V4 reading (no branch), those dry runs must declare the path they actually traverse. NC-E03-NOT-HELD still needs the switch, because continuing past PL means writing with no document lock, a path V2.1 8 does not define.
rulings.reasoning: V2.1 13.1 defines the criterion on 'the non-governing dry runs of that scenario', and AR2-42 makes it per scenario. The declared residual of 13.1 covers paths that 'cannot be exercised by the warm-up', while these refusal and abort paths can be exercised by a dry run. A dry run that follows another path does not measure scenario X's governed window. A harness switch is within the characterization-build concept that AR3-01 already rules.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-03: contribution of the KS-* seam-failure scenarios to group KS
rulings.recommendation: RULE. KS-* add no PASS to KS or SC-A. Under AR2-08, KS PASS comes only from S-1 and S-2 in CONTROLS_EXERCISED, and PA-1.3 defines KS as the seams with comparators S-1..S-3, which a PRE-WRITE or POST-WRITE abort never reaches. The V2.1 31 listing of KS-* for the S-1..S-3 row is met by the scenario class existing (31 design check 1); the row's minimum catalog requirement (clean runs, writers at X1..X4, single-field mutations) does not name seam failures. Keep the KS and SC-A membership in CONTRACT_ASSIGNED_GROUPS as evidence only, with an explicit extension of AR3-06 to 'scenario classes the contract lists for a group whose controls the scenario cannot reach by design'. Keep GROUP AB: S-5 adjudicates the rollback. Keep KR (NO_VERDICT, E-14/E-15). Adjudicate the SEAM typed failure as EXPECTED_PROCEDURAL_RESULT (V2.2 PA-3). A mismatch (wrong type, a write after a PRE-WRITE failure, no abort) is recorded as a seam-contract finding against KS (V2.1 15.3, 15.4) that prevents KS PASS and never adds to it. Lift the AQ-V4-03 blocker from the three KS-*. If the Architect wants KS PASS credit for failure typing, that needs a registry control for it, which means a contract amendment.
rulings.reasoning: No registry control adjudicates seam failure typing, and AR2-08 allows PASS coverage only through controls exercised. S-5 already gives the rollback half of the KS-* purpose (V2.1 26.3) a PASS-bearing control in AB. The failure-typing half is a design requirement of section 15 and can only be checked procedurally. Counting a mismatch against KS keeps the fail-closed intent of AR2-08 and V2.1 3.2 without inventing PASS credit.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-04: whether E6-C4 blocks the catalog seal given AR3-26
rulings.recommendation: RULE: E6-C4 does not block the catalog seal, so the V4 reading holds. Consequences to record: NC-S5-O6 stays DRAFT, not runnable as governing, in the sealed catalog. The S-5 deliberate-violation cell is NEGATIVE_CONTROL_NOT_EVALUATED (AR3-03), and V2.1 31 check 2 for S-5 must be recorded as unmet, or with a sealed reason, at acceptance. A later declaration is a new scenario version and therefore, since the catalog is sealed at artifact level (AR3-25), a new catalog and baseline version. The Architect should also consider revising the E-06 clause of AR3-04. The Wr-OCT write at Y1 opens and closes between the PS and PV sampling points of V2.1 4.2, so E-06 = PASS at every sampling point can be determined without E6-C4. This is the same blind-spot reasoning V4 applies to KS-SL1-TX-MISMATCH. Such a revision would remove the E6-C4 blocker and the uncovered S-5 cell.
rulings.reasoning: AR3-26 is exhaustive: 'bloquean el sello del catálogo solo K-3 ..., K-8 y los dictámenes del Arquitecto'. E6-C4 is none of these. It is itself an EXPLORATORY_NON_GOVERNING scenario of this catalog, which can run only after the baseline, so making it a seal blocker would be circular (V2.1 26.2: exploratory results are never promoted). The E-06 UNKNOWN conditions of 4.2 are not met when the count is the same at PS and PV and the transaction is closed between the samples.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-06: governing scenarios on the characterization build, and two build identities in the tuple
rulings.recommendation: RULE: accept, with conditions. Governing runs on a characterization build are contract-grounded for injections that need I-14 injection points: V2.1 10.6 puts the writers 'at a deterministic injection point of a characterization build of the verifier', SC-A cells are 'guarantee-bearing', and 4.3 row I-14 is 'usable only in characterization builds'. V2.1 2 requires every BUILD_BOUND field to equal the baseline, so the baseline must carry the characterization build as its own set of BUILD_BOUND values, and each run is compared with the entries of its declared BUILD_UNDER_TEST. Conditions: (1) CHARACTERIZATION_TUPLE replaces every build-dependent field with its own value: Plugin and harness DLL hashes, the manifest build layer (the E-10 exact set per 12.3 and the WUM set per 13.1), the warm-up definition if it differs, and the qualification records of that build per 4.3. The instruments must be qualified on it or a sealed transfer ruled, and Q-I14 moves to it (BA04V4-01). (2) The equivalence 'differs only by harness switches disabled by default' is verified and recorded, for example product assemblies byte-identical with the switches in separate harness assemblies, or a reviewed diff. This matters because the E04, LOCK_MODE and HOST_DEFAULT_MAP pins are derived on the characterization build and applied to 65 PRODUCT_BUILD governing runs, and the E4-VAL-R1 membership post-check stays the safeguard. (3) Scenarios whose injections need no switch stay on PRODUCT_BUILD (V4 1.2). (4) The EV-L/EV-V build alignment follows AQ-V4-01 (V2.1 27.5). Blocks: the catalog candidate (C-3), BA-07 manifest custody, and BA-08 K-10 / BA-09 W-7.
rulings.reasoning: The contract foresees characterization builds for the scan experiment and makes harness DLL identities BUILD_BOUND. It is silent on two coexisting baseline builds, so an explicit ruling is needed. Without the conditions, E-10's exact set equality and the requirement that qualification be on the exact build make every characterization-build run refused or unable to reach PASS.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-14: failure-path event classes (the EVM_INCOMPLETE residual) in governing abort scenarios
rulings.recommendation: RULE: no expectation changes. None of the twenty listed scenarios adjudicates a failure-path event class, for these reasons. (a) Phase A is evaluated at PV over the events from the opening of T_M to PV (V2.1 5 PV row, V2.1 8 sequence, V2.1 14 table), and in the PV-reach scenarios the abort follows the PV evaluation. (b) Events from the end of the PV evaluation onward, including an Abort() after PV and U-6b's ended transaction and failed Commit(), fall in the commit-boundary interval, which is logged and not adjudicated (V2.1 9, NG-19b). (c) PREPARE-W imports and their failures are phase 0, which is log only. (d) REACH PS/PW scenarios (the KS-* and PW-* families, NC-CLONE-REPLACE, AB-AFTER-PREPARE-W, U-1, PR-SOURCE-SWAP-NEG-COPY) never reach PV, so phase A is NOT_EVALUATED (AR2-25), even for the partial writes of KS-SL1-POSTWRITE. (e) ABORT-VERIFY reads run after the abort, in a fresh read-only transaction outside every phase. EVM_INCOMPLETE (V2.2 PA-10) is a classification of phase-A adjudication in validation and cannot arise from these classes. Required only: each listed scenario's EXPECTED_EVENTS should state that post-PV and post-abort events are logged and not adjudicated. The BA-06 V4 row stays a disclosed EVM-completeness residual (OC-ABV-READ is already excluded as 'failure path only; outside f(plan)').
rulings.reasoning: The phase windows of V2.1 5, 8, 9 and 14 put every failure-path event class named by BA-06 V4 section 5 outside the adjudicated domain in time. A ruling is needed only for the reading that the pre-V0 boundary of an aborted run runs from the end of PV to Abort(). The catalog's expectations already treat phase A as NOT_EVALUATED where PV is not reached.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-08: CONTEXT members in EXPECTED_AFTER_ABORT
rulings.recommendation: RULE that every member of the PRE_COMMAND_STATE_RECORD, CONTEXT included (CONTEXT_VARIABLE and REFERENCE), is part of EXPECTED_AFTER_ABORT and is compared exactly by ABORT-VERIFY. The contract fixes this; it is not a kind-baseline choice. So BA-08 V4's proposed answer is endorsed for ABORT-VERIFY. The E-08 domain is the kind baseline's. Comparing the REFERENCE members at PS/PV is admissible and recommended, because they feed SL-R. Leaving the CONTEXT_VARIABLE members out of E-08 is admissible only with a disclosure: a context change between capture and PV would then show up as an S-comparison difference (O4) instead of a class-A abort. Adding them to E-08 is recommended. BA-05 2.3.5 must be reworded (BA05V4-02).
rulings.reasoning: V2.1 11: EXPECTED_AFTER_ABORT = PRE_COMMAND_STATE_RECORD + EXACT PREPARE_RESIDUE_MANIFEST. 11.3 'Consequence ... and nothing else', and the case 'unexpected mutation: any change to an element of the record => O6'. 11.2: exact match => O2. AR3-11 conditions 2 and 3 put the ST-13 set and the context keys into the record, so they are elements of the record. Comparing them is fail-closed without false O6, because the product writes no context variable and never touches the source reference (no Clayer or SetSystemVariable writes under src at 3375aadb). E-08 is defined as the re-observation of the 11.1 read-set (V2.1 5 PS/PV rows; the class table 'E8 ... 5, 11.1'), and context variables are not listed in 11.1, so the contract leaves E-08's coverage of them to the kind baseline.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-09: plot style name for ST-13
rulings.recommendation: RULE the declared-gap option. FPSPEC-V1 adds no plot-style field, and the gap stays declared in the kind baseline for CT-21D, on three conditions: (1) BA-08 binds PSTYLEMODE = 1 to the pinned fixture bytes and verifies it in the fixture conformance record, or captures PSTYLEMODE as a CONTEXT_VARIABLE member; (2) any governing run on a drawing with named plot styles (PSTYLEMODE = 0) makes SL-R UNKNOWN (O5), never EQUAL; (3) the gap is disclosed among the Owner Act 2 coverage limits (BA-05 2.4 with BA-08 section 11 rule 1). A future fixture or kind with STB needs a table change before the BA-05 seal (2.6), or FPSPEC-V2 after it.
rulings.reasoning: The canonical ENTITY content of V2.1 28.1 does not list a plot style name, so BA-05 is not required to type it. AR2-34 accepted a declared coverage boundary. V17 ST-13 (as cited in BA-08 V4 line 226) makes PlotStyleName an independent value only under STB; under CTB it derives from Color, which is typed and compared. V2.1 11.1 ('never silently omitted') requires the fail-closed guard for STB drawings. Adding the field now would need host characterization of what the host reports under CTB, and would change every ENTITY_* digest with no benefit for CT-21D.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-10: source of dimension overrides
rulings.recommendation: RULE that `overrides` is the stored override set: the typed values of the DSTYLE section of the entity's ACAD extended data, as an RB sequence in host order (BA-05 V4 2.3.2). It is not an effective value compared with the style. Conditions before the BA-05 candidate: the census (section 5 step 5) and the I-12 qualification confirm, on the exact build, the storage location, the host order, and whether the host stores or drops an override equal to the style value. BA-08's oracle predicts the stored set under that characterized behaviour. Handle-valued overrides stay UNKNOWN (EV-83) and are disclosed. A different storage changes the table before the seal (2.6).
rulings.reasoning: V2.1 28.1 fingerprints stored state: exact stored text, stored case, and 'raw stored bytes', which AR3-21 reads as the stored ResultBuffer. An effective reading would fold style-record values into every dimension digest. That would double the coverage of SYMBOL_RECORD_DIMSTYLE, make a style change alter dimension digests (misattributing an unexpected mutation), and hide an override equal to the style value, which is real stored state. V2.1 28.2 compares the persisted typed form read by the authoritative reader, and the persisted form of an override is the stored extended data. The product's eight overrides (LateralHeaderDrawer.cs:365-372 at 3375aadb: DIMSCALE, DIMTXT, DIMASZ, DIMEXE, DIMEXO, DIMGAP, DIMTAD, DIMDEC) are all real or integer values, none handle-valued, so the EV-83 rule does not make the product's own dimensions UNKNOWN.

rulings.item: Handle keys of REFERENCE members inside the PRE_COMMAND_STATE_RECORD (BA05V4-01) against V2.1 28.1 exclusions
rulings.recommendation: Accept it as the Architect's reading of V2.1 28.1, with the same scope as the ENUMERATION exception (within one session, excluded from the cross-session determinism control of 28.3). Require BA-05 to disclose it in section 7 with this decision id.
rulings.reasoning: AR3-11 condition 2 needs the source reference identified inside the record, and a handle is its only stable in-session identity. The PCSR already carries handle ENUMERATION digests, so it was never cross-session deterministic. The deviation is textual, but it relaxes a normative exclusion list, so it needs a recorded decision rather than an implementer edit.

rulings.item: Slot-unit instantiation rule (3.3.1) and the numerical behaviour of SV-11
rulings.recommendation: Accept 3.3.1 as written. Record that SV-11 is intended to reject a comparator that computes the angle as acos of the dot product in binary64: such a comparator returns EQUAL at small slots, where the exact-arithmetic instance is DIFFERENT. Conformant comparators must compute the angle stably (for example atan2(|a x b|, a.b)).
rulings.reasoning: In scratch, SV-06, 07, 10 and 11 were instantiated as the nearest binary64 values at three slot magnitudes. All instances are valid under the exact check and give the declared results. SV-07 separates absolute from relative, SV-10 separates wrapped from unwrapped, and SV-11 separates stable from acos-based comparators. A degenerate slot below about 4.4e-16 makes SV-07 INVALID, and 3.3.1 already reports that (never PASS).

findings.evidence: §9: 'The learning corpus is the set of isolated micro-scenarios … (EV-L-OC-*, 16 of them …), plus EV-L-COMPOSED, … sealed by hash'. §3.3: 'EV-L-COMPOSED checks the composition rule f(plan) of section 11 on a full mirror of FX-1F'. V2.1 14.3: 'Learning uses only micro-scenarios that isolate single operations'. V2.1 27.2 step 2: 'each operation category is executed in isolation'. V2.1 27.3: the corpus is 'the set of micro-scenarios'. A composition check before the freeze is a validation-type check inside learning, which strains V2.1 14.3 and 27.1 ('The same run never teaches and validates').
findings.required_fix: Either take EV-L-COMPOSED out of the learning corpus and LEARNING_CORPUS_HASH, for example as a non-governing composition check against the DRAFT or UNDER_REVIEW model that contributes no entry, or as a check deferred to validation. Or ask the Architect to rule it admissible, with the conditions that it contributes no model entry and that any of its events that no isolated entry explains are recorded as UNEXPLAINED_EVENTS (V2.1 27.2 step 4). Align BA-04 V4 EV-L-COMPOSED with the choice.

(1) Answer AQ-V4-11 at the same time, adopting the CQ-01 and CQ-06 readings; the other contract questions are answered or deferred without any change to the inventory (see the AQ-V4-11 rulings below). (2) State that the approval of the trace plan covers its use of the AR3-01 mode on the characterization build for the trace dry runs (non-governing by design, V2.1 21.1). Record the build-equivalence limit of BA06V4-N03 in the approval or require it in the candidate version. (3) The four MINOR findings (BA06V4-N01..N04) go into the candidate version (a narrow V4.1), with an exact line-level delta check before the candidate ruling. Because none of them changes the content of the inventory or of the trace plan, STATIC_REVIEWED carries over.
rulings.reasoning: Every AR3-22 item is present and correct in the bytes. DC-04 is in §5, DC-49 in §3.3 (C-26 included) and DC-51 in §12 as EVM_STATUS, the contract's own name (V2.2 PA-2). DC-01 is re-resolved as one lock from PL to V1 (X-01; V2.1 3.4 P-L3, 5, 8, 11; AR2-11). Each AMB-nn cites an outside clause that exists and says what is cited, or is routed to CQ-01..CQ-07. DC-47 is resolved by V2.1 7.1 and 11.3, with C-98 amended. The item (10) anchor is cited as recorded. INVENTORY_REVIEW_RECORDS is landed and cited by the EVM_FROZEN pin (BA-07 V4 and BA-11 V4). There was no new compilation. The trace plan meets conditions 3 and 4: BA06-C1 checks the columns against the 9 classes of §10.2; every seam entry point has a row, plus the ORCH row; reconciliation now covers every operation instance from P0 to PC; the T-2 fallback and the success-path-only limit are declared. The evidence is sound: 26/26 hashes, 12/12 checks byte-identical, V3 evidence and contract files unchanged, and no code claim wrong in more than 40 checked lines. The two MAJOR findings of V3 are closed. What remains is textual (N01, N02), a declared-limit gap (N03), and a construct carried from V3 (N04). Condition 1 matters because the inventory rests on the CQ-01 reading (OC-LIB-ACQ and the PREPARE-W checks are the orchestrator's; otherwise C-186 would require a micro-scenario for an SL-5 side-database load) and on the CQ-06 reading (OC-ENVELOPE has no SL-4 instance). rulings.item: AQ-V4-11, condition 5 of PA-11 (product part): does a union built by the critic satisfy 'the reviewer did not compile or create the inventory'?
rulings.recommendation: ACCEPT condition 5 for the product part, and record three limitations: (i) compliance with 'read nothing else' is shown by the outputs, not by a tool log; (ii) the fidelity of the published task texts rests on the implementer's read-only extraction from local run records, and TI-EV cannot be reproduced from the repository; (iii) the task framing was written by the implementer (the seam-contract paraphrase, the entry points and the REACH path). It is scope, not inventory, and the contract part was compiled independently from verbatim fragments (AR2-37).
rulings.reasoning: The inventory that the reviewer must not have compiled is the starting input, the implementer's BA-06 V1 (PA-11: 'the starting input, not the completeness authority'). The phase-1 ruling, step 2 (line 120), asks for an independent static review by someone who did not compile the inventory and did not see it, followed by a resolved difference log. V24-N2, text pre-approved by the Architect, reads condition 6 as 'the differences between the static reviewers and the critic are resolved explicitly', so the Architect already treats the critic as part of the review. The published task texts show the BLIND rule in B1a, B1b and the critic, forbidding .codex and D:\Documentos, where V1 lived. The critic's input is exactly B1a and B1b (reproduced by BA06-C10). Adopting the reviewers' union as §3.1 is the intended use of a review output, and the differences with V1 are logged in D-01..D-16.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-11 / CQ-01: does SL-5's 'fresh acquire' only name the input SL-5 consumes, and are the PREPARE-W checks the orchestrator's?
rulings.recommendation: RULE yes to both; adopt the BA-06 reading. No change to the bytes.
rulings.reasoning: The acquisition belongs to PREPARE-R: V2.1 6 ('library input identity and cache freshness (section 19.1)' is PREPARE-R content); V2.1 5 row PR (the LibraryInputRecord); V2.1 19.1 step 5 ('invalidate explicitly in PREPARE-R before the acquire'); steps 4 and 6 ('open the library Database from the private copy'; 'SL-5 receives the opened Database, not a path to the original source'). V2.1 15.8 P-4 ('a fresh-acquire library path (SL-5)') names the importer's input. SL-5 holds only the Database, so it cannot re-hash the copy file or revalidate the generation id of the LibraryInputRecord. The UNKNOWN row of V2.1 19.1 ('an import result not confirmed by a re-query and a fingerprint') puts that confirmation outside the importer. ALT-21D V4 3.3 item 1 names 'the product' (the orchestrating command) for the re-observation.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-11 / CQ-02: when is the cloning-mode allow-list checked?
rulings.recommendation: RULE: adopt the BA-06 reading. The importer has a fixed declaration of its cloning mode, checked against the allow-list before PREPARE-W starts, and every structured result re-declares the mode. A result that declares another mode is the cloning FAIL; the run then stops, and ABORT-VERIFY gives O2 or O6. The allow-list is {DuplicateRecordCloning.Ignore} plus any equivalent proven by CLONE_NON_REPLACE_CONTROL.
rulings.reasoning: V2.1 7.1 has two sentences, 'declare the mode it used in its structured result' and 'PREPARE-W does not start unless the declared mode is on the allow-list'. They can only both hold if a declaration exists before the first import and is re-declared per result. 'If the cloning policy differs … FAIL' and 'replacement is never silently permitted' (7.1) settle the mismatch. The stop and the outcome follow V2.1 7 ('the run stops; ABORT-VERIFY…') and 17.2 rows 3 and 4. The inventory does not depend on this answer.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-11 / CQ-03: outcomes of (i) a mismatch of the copy re-hash before the first import, (ii) a failed generation-id revalidation, (iii) a mismatch of the copy re-hash after the run
rulings.recommendation: (i) and (ii), when they occur before the first import: RULE O1 by V2.1 17.2 row 2. After at least one import: O2 or O6 by ABORT-VERIFY (rows 3 and 4), which is the 'O2 with the residue produced so far' of V2.1 19.1. (iii) DEFER: no outcome row applies after CP, and settling it needs a reviewed amendment. It blocks no BA-06 content and no BA-04 V4 scenario; PR-SOURCE-SWAP-NEG-COPY places the mismatch after the first import.
rulings.reasoning: The LibraryInputRecord and the generation id are PREPARE-R content (V2.1 6), and 'the copy hash differs from the record' is an UNKNOWN of the acquisition (V2.1 19.1 UNKNOWN row). Before any product write, row 2 ('a PREPARE-R FAIL or UNKNOWN … before any product write') is the first row that matches. ALT-21D V4 3.3 item 2 gives the same outcome for the sibling case ('no product write has occurred' => O1 REFUSED). Row 3 needs a PREPARE-W write. CP is the only completion point (V2.1 5), so a check after the run cannot change O1..O7 without an amendment.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-11 / CQ-04: may a seam open and close a nested transaction inside T_M?
rulings.recommendation: DEFER to the seam implementation review (EXEC-3, P-1..P-5). Record the BA-06 baseline reading: no nested transaction is planned, and one observed in E2 creates a new operation class and reopens its review (V2.4). No change to the bytes.
rulings.reasoning: V2.1 15.3 does not forbid a nested StartTransaction. V2.1 4.2 requires 'no nested transaction' only at PV, and declares transactions that start and end between two samples a blind spot. Forbidding them outright would add a static guard, which is a contract amendment. The design-time inventory does not depend on the answer.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-11 / CQ-05: E-06 second source, logging of IsTopTransaction, and owner of the typed authority
rulings.recommendation: RULE on the logging: the log records the three-valued result (YES, NO or UNKNOWN) and a sequence number. DEFER to the qualification of I-07 (E6-C5) and to the implementation review whether 'own bookkeeping' is a mandatory second source and who owns the implementation of the authority.
rulings.reasoning: In V2.1 4.2, 'records the boolean result' stands in contrast to 'never used as a log key' for the pointer. The UNKNOWN condition 'IsTopTransaction cannot decide' can only be applied if UNKNOWN can be recorded. The text makes no single source mandatory; the UNKNOWN rule applies when two sources that are present disagree. None of this changes the inventory.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-11 / CQ-06: does SL-4 write and read back an envelope, and what is 'support' of the fresh reread?
rulings.recommendation: RULE: adopt the BA-06 reading. SL-4 writes no envelope. SL-1 and SL-2 support the reread by writing the envelope where RackBlockData.Read and RackBlockFinder.ScanEnvelopes find it, and by returning the handles required by V2.1 15.4. This confirms that OC-ENVELOPE has no SL-4 instance.
rulings.reasoning: V2.1 10.2 lists 'each sibling's authored envelope', and 25.7 lists 'envelopes' per selected view. V2.1 15.7 reads envelopes through ScanEnvelopes, which scans block table records ('skips layouts, anonymous and xref records'), and through RackBlockData.Read. At 3375aadb the product stores the envelope in the extension dictionary of the definition (RackBlockData.cs:16, 27-51). The 15.3 clause 'exact authored payload' therefore binds SL-4 vacuously.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-11 / CQ-07: seam-design details (deterministic result, naming actor, InvalidPlan and InvalidEnvelope criteria, MissingInstances and Diagnostic, host-generated objects, SL-4 property list)
rulings.recommendation: DEFER to the seam implementation review (EXEC-3; P-1..P-6), except for two points the contract already settles, which the Architect can record now. (a) A name that the sanitizer reduces to empty is InvalidBlockName (PRE-WRITE) in the seam (V2.1 15.4, 15.5), and PREPARE-R refuses the run with O1 when its expected effective name is empty (V2.1 6: every rejection known from these inputs occurs in PREPARE-R as a clean O1). (b) Host-generated objects, such as the anonymous dimension blocks, stay the §5 residual until the implementation review; BA-05 V4 2.4 excludes anonymous BTRs as definitions.
rulings.reasoning: None of these points changes an operation, class or trace cell of the design-time inventory. The contract (15.3-15.6) leaves them as seam-design choices.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-01, BA-06 part (CQ-08 and the build and controls of the learning runs EV-L-*)
rulings.recommendation: RULE that E-12 phases A and C are recorded, not enforced, in EV-L-*. This is contract-grounded by V2.1 27.2 and V2.2 PA-2 (without a FROZEN EVM, E12-V is NOT_EVALUATED). For the rest, the contract supports two options. (a) Preferred: run EV-L-* on the exact product build, with every other control under the governing policy: E-03 under the LOCK_MODE pin chosen from the LK-* runs, E-04 under its admitted-set pin, and S-1..S-3 evaluated where the run reaches VERIFY with HOST_DEFAULT_MAP and K-3 fixed (AR3-26), otherwise NOT_EVALUATED. CQ-08 is then moot. (b) If the Architect keeps the characterization build, the BA-06 reading 'no tuple change' needs an explicit Architect ruling, not a reading of the text. That ruling should require a recorded equivalence in the learning and REVIEWED records: same source SHA, harness switches off, no I-14 writer loaded or armed. Blocks: the 17 EV-L-* scenarios (DRAFT) and prerequisite (2) of the BA-06 candidate. It does not block STATIC_REVIEWED.
rulings.reasoning: AR3-01 covers only E4-LEARN-R1-* and LK-*, and states that it does not change the phase policy of governing runs, which EV-L-* are. V2.1 14.3 and 27.5 treat a change of the tuple, the build included, as requiring a new model version, review and revalidation. V2.1 27.2 step 2 requires a 'manifest-attested' environment with 'no adversarial probes', while V2.1 4.3 row I-14 says the writers are 'usable only in characterization builds'. So nothing in the text makes a characterization-build EVM valid for validation on the product build without a ruling.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-14: event classes of failure paths (EVM_INCOMPLETE residual) in governing abort scenarios
rulings.recommendation: RULE the contract consequence and choose a mitigation. The consequence (V2.2 PA-10) is that an event class of an abort path that the frozen EVM does not explain is EVM_INCOMPLETE: never a host verdict, and it requires a new model version, review and revalidation. So an abort scenario that meets one cannot give an E12-V PASS. Preferred mitigation: learn the rollback of Abort() after writes as a variant of the existing class OC-TM. C-05 is an inventoried operation, and V2.1 27.2 steps 1-2 require isolated micro-scenarios of every primitive used. This means a §3.3 and §9 wording change in BA-06 V4.1 and a matching EV-L-OC-TM variant in BA-04; the §5 residual then shrinks to the host events of the failing call itself. In either case, BA-04 abort scenarios declare through a conditional rule that such a finding is recorded and routed to a model revision, not to a group verdict. If the Architect prefers not to change BA-06, DEFER. That blocks the BA-04 candidate (BA-11 V4 row BA-04) but not BA-06 STATIC_REVIEWED, because the learning corpus is not part of the reviewed inventory.
rulings.reasoning: EV-L-OC-TM learns start, commit and abort of an empty T_M on FX-SCRATCH. The rollback events of an abort after partial writes are therefore not learned, and the trace plan declares failure paths untraced (§7 limit 3). PA-10 fixes the consequence. The contract offers no exemption for failure paths in phase A.

findings.location: s5 'amendment and versioning' row (line 132); s5.1 field supersedes (line 147); s6.1 supersededBy (line 204); s6.2 step 5 (line 228); s7 pin use precondition (line 272)
findings.claim: Nothing says that a pin slot holds one live value. The verifier accepts two ratified, anchored pin records for the same slot, each consumed by governing runs, with no SUPERSEDED entry. A pin record's supersedes field is never checked against the log. Nothing restricts superseding a pin that governing runs have already consumed.
findings.evidence:
- Line 132 allows a new pin version at any time.
- supersedes (line 147) and SUPERSEDED/supersededBy (line 204) are not tied together by any check.
- The use precondition (line 272) only requires the consumed pin to be anchored and not SUPERSEDED or REVOKED before u, and step 5 has no slot check.
- Independent simulation (my own verifier written from the V4 text): two LOCK_MODE pin records, the second with supersedes = the first, both ratified by the Coordinator and the Architect and both anchored, with no SUPERSEDED entry. Run R5 consumes the old value and run R6 the new one. Result: PASS_WITH_DECLARED_LIMITS.
- Authority: AR2-16 (a pin is one named slot with its value); AR2-11 ('el pin no se revisa por retrospectiva'); AR2-17 and AR3-26 (fixed before the first governing run that uses it); V2.1 27.5 (a run under an older model version is not evidence for the newer one); V2.1 21.3 (no cherry-picking).
findings.required_fix:
In 6.2 step 5 and section 7:
(1) At every index, allow at most one live pin (not SUPERSEDED, not REVOKED) per (baselineVersion, pinSlot). A PIN_RECORDED for a slot that already has a live pin is legal only if its record's supersedes names that pin, and the predecessor's SUPERSEDED entry (supersededBy = the new hash) is appended before any IN_USE. Any other case is a violation with a new code.
(2) Check the record's supersedes against the SUPERSEDED/supersededBy pair.
(3) State that a pin already consumed by a governing run may be superseded only where the contract allows it: never for E04_ADMITTED_SET (AR2-11); for EVM_FROZEN, runs under the predecessor are not evidence for the successor (V2.1 27.5). IN_USE pinRecordHashes attributes each run to the version it consumed.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-12: how to read the pin state machine, and whether pins and the manifest carry over to a new baseline version (BA-07 V4)
rulings.recommendation:
(1) Pin state machine: ACCEPT the V4 reading.
- RECORDED is the content-addressed pin record and has no custody entry of its own.
- RATIFIED means both ratification records exist. PIN_RECORDED (APPROVAL_ROLE) is appended only then, and it cites both.
- ANCHORED is derived.
Add to step 5 that:
- the two records are one COORDINATOR and one ARCHITECT, decision RATIFIED, subjectKind PIN, subject = the pinSlot, subjectHash = the pin-record hash;
- the record's baselineVersion is the version in force;
- a slot has at most one live pin (BA07-V4-01).
(2) Carry-over: DO NOT accept the fail-open default.
- A pin is usable only under the baseline version named in its record.
- Carrying a pin over to v<k+1> means writing a new pin version for v<k+1> (the same value is allowed; supersedes = the old record), with its own two ratifications and a PIN_RECORDED, followed by SUPERSEDED of the old pin, all before the first governing use under v<k+1>.
- Without that record, the pin is not usable.
- The manifest is bound to the tuple (EXEC-11), not to the baseline. It stays usable under v<k+1> only when the ruling that approves the new version records that BA-07 and every tuple field are unchanged. Otherwise it is REVOKED (SUPERSEDED_BY_RULING) and captured again.
- Every such SUPERSEDED or REVOKED entry is appended before the first anchor of v<k+1>: extend the three-entry sequence of section 8 and set h to the last of these entries.
rulings.reasoning:
- AR3-23 says the ratification records are 'citados por PIN_RECORDED', so PIN_RECORDED must follow both ratifications.
- AR2-16 asks for one 'entrada de custodia en BA-07', which that entry satisfies.
- V2.2 PA-13 separation holds: PIN_RECORDED is the approval entry and ANCHOR_RECORDED is the custody entry.
- A pin fills a slot of one sealed catalog (AR2-16), and the record's baselineVersion names that catalog (5.1).
- AR2-43 ('never a silent change'), V2.1 21.3 (a changed scenario, contract or model is a new version) and V2.1 27.5 rule out an implicit carry-over.
- V2.1 29.1 binds the manifest to the tuple.
- The simulation shows that the draft reading lets a run under v2 consume v1 pins with a clean verification (BA07-V4-02). Placing the revocations before the new anchor closes that window without any new event type.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-13 (a) = Q-A1: do CONTRACT_ASSIGNED_GROUPS enter N_strict?
rulings.recommendation:
NO. Contract-assigned groups do not enter N_strict:
- PR-CLOSURE-COMPLETENESS stays under EVIDENCE;
- the X7 and residual cells keep the N_strict of their GROUPS_SERVED.
In AR3-24, 'sirve grupos A o B' reads as GROUPS_SERVED, which AR3-06 requires to be exactly the AR2-08 derivation (checked mechanically). If the Coordinator wants detection power on qualification scenarios, it can raise EVIDENCE_REPETITION as its own engineering choice.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-13 (b): the intent of CHAR_RUNS. (i) Does it need its own Owner pair? (ii) For HDM-CHAR, N_A at the pinned configuration only, or for every key configuration?
rulings.recommendation:
(i) ACCEPT the derived N_c (N_A today); no new Owner question. Conditions:
- Q-O1 keeps disclosing that the same pair sizes these runs (it does);
- BA-10 states that a missed behaviour fails closed.
(ii) ACCEPT N_A runs at the pinned key configuration, but replace 'at least one' with EXACTLY one informative run per varied key, so that the sealed plan is determinate and no unnamed authority can add runs. The HOST_DEFAULT_MAP pin record marks the varied-key entries as informative, and a governing lookup that resolves to one of them is UNKNOWN (O5 path), so an entry backed by a single run never carries governing weight.
rulings.reasoning:
- V2.1 21.7 has MUST_FIX rows for group repetitions, determinism, clean runs, attempts and the machine label. Characterization runs are NON_GOVERNING and carry no group verdict (V2.1 21.1; AR2-11; AR3-01), so no separate row applies.
- BA10-V3-08 allowed 'state the intent ... or give them their own parameter', and V4 states the intent.
- A miss is fail-closed:
  - E-04 refuses a member outside the admitted set, and the E4 group is UNKNOWN on a membership miss (AR2-11);
  - NO_CANDIDATE gives LK = FAIL (V2.1 3.4);
  - a missing key tuple is UNKNOWN (AR3-11 condition 4; BA-08 V4 HDM-5).
- Every governing run presents the pinned key values (BA-08 V4 HDM-4, and section 12 requires them equal in every template), so the intent is only needed at that configuration.
- The other reading costs +756 non-governing runs at row1 (memo E.2).
- The defensive lookup rule makes the claim that the varied-key entries are 'outside the intent' enforceable.

rulings.item: When may the cost memo and Q-O1..Q-O5 go to the Owner (AR3-24)?
rulings.recommendation: After the Architect rules on AQ-V4-13 and after the memo's attribution is corrected (BA10-V4-03). AQ-V4-01 need not block it: its size is disclosed in memo block F.

rulings.item: Is BA-10 V4 symbolic, and does it choose no Owner or Coordinator value?
rulings.recommendation: Yes, on both counts.
rulings.reasoning: The bytes contain no count, no K, no V(s) and no total taken from the catalog; the only numbers are identifiers and clause numbers. Every value is UNSET. EVIDENCE_REPETITION is marked as a proposal for the Coordinator. PARAM-05 is a proposal for confirmation by the Owner or the CAD manager. The illustrative figures live only in the non-sealed memo. The only authority-wording defects are BA10-V4-03 (in the memo) and BA10-V4-02 (a gate in BA-11).

findings.location: section 4, paragraph 'Dry-run mode' (line 76) and paragraph 'Consequences' (line 80)
findings.claim: Each WU-DRY-X replays 'the plan, fixture specification, injections and designed stimuli of X', and its measured expectation is 'no assembly-load event inside the governed window'. A load found by a dry run is a design finding, fixed by revising the warm-up or by 'preloading the dependent assembly'.
findings.evidence:
Four governing scenarios inject a CANARY_LOAD (variant assembly) inside the governed window:
- NC-E11M-PV and AB-AFTER-MUTATION: 'between PS and PV';
- NC-E11M-PC and U-5: X7, which is before PC and so inside the E-11M window (V2.1 13.2: events from subscription to PC).
Their dry runs (WU-DRY-NC-E11M-PV, WU-DRY-NC-E11M-PC, WU-DRY-AB-AFTER-MUTATION, WU-DRY-U-5) carry the same injection, 'replay its path as a load-path stimulus', and declare E11M 'no assembly-load event inside the governed window ... a load is an E-11M finding (class B) and a design finding'. The canary load is itself such an event, so the criterion of V2.1 13.1 can never be met for these four scenarios. BA-09 section 4's own remedy, preloading the dependent assembly, would preload the canary in the warm-up. The canary would then no longer be a first-time load in the governing runs, and the E-11M negative controls NC-E11M-PV/PC, the U-5 E-11M FAIL (AR3-09) and the AB-AFTER-MUTATION violation (AR3-05) would be neutralized. BA-09 V4 has no text about designed loads: no occurrence of 'canary'.

findings.claim: The keys of HOST_DEFAULT_MAP include 'the current text style and dimension style, all captured in the PRE_COMMAND_STATE_RECORD'. The row captures only the seven variables CLAYER..CPLOTSTYLE as CONTEXT_VARIABLE members, and gives the style 'identities' through their STYLE and DIMSTYLE records in the row 'symbol tables'.
findings.evidence: A SYMBOL_RECORD_STYLE or SYMBOL_RECORD_DIMSTYLE member (memberKey READ_SET|STYLE|<name>, BA-05 V4 2.3.5) does not say that its record is the current one. The same row adds other STYLE members: the transitive records of the current dimension style (its DIMTXSTY text style) and the closure's pre-existing text styles. No member records TEXTSTYLE or DIMSTYLE. BA-05 V4 CONTEXT_VARIABLE accepts any variable 'as the kind baseline lists it', but BA-08 lists only the seven. Under HDM-2 ('A key the record cannot read is UNKNOWN, and so is every attribute looked up with it'), the style part of the key tuple cannot be formed without ambiguity, so HOST_DEFAULT_MAP lookups keyed on it fall to UNKNOWN. - add every other view through RACKEDITAR, without changing any input.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-04: does E6-C4 block the catalog seal, given AR3-26?
rulings.recommendation:
The reading holds for the seal. E6-C4 is not a catalog seal blocker; NC-S5-O6 stays DRAFT, and so cannot run as governing.

The ruling must also settle the BASELINE_READY consequence. NC-S5-O6 is the only negative control of S5, which is class A and mandatory (BA-02b V4 section 2, S5 row). With it undeclared, S5 has no declared deliberate-violation scenario, so V2.1 31 check 2 and BA-02b rule 7 (phase-1 ruling B) fail for S5. Preferred fix: replace 'BLOCKED_BY E6-C4' with a registered conditional expectation for E-06 keyed on the recorded E6-C4 result of the exact build, following the AR2-12 / AR3-03 pattern. Every other part of AR3-04 stays as it is: E-08 FAIL at PV unconditional, E-12 phase A conditional on the witness, O6/NOT_RUNNABLE by CER-PERSIST. NC-S5-O6 then needs only K-3 to be sealed as a conditional negative control, and S5 is COVERED_DRAFT_CONDITIONAL, then NEGATIVE_CONTROL_NOT_EVALUATED at acceptance unless its detection branch fires (rule 5).

If the Architect keeps AR3-04 as it is, record explicitly that BASELINE_READY waits for a new BA-04 version once E6-C4 is characterized. That version cascades to BA-02b and BA-11 and makes a new baseline version.
rulings.reasoning:
AR3-26 is a closed list: K-3, K-8 and the Architect's rulings. E6-C4 is exploratory host evidence: V2.1 4.3 lists it outside the I-07 acceptance criteria, and BA-02b R07 marks it EXPLORATORY_NON_GOVERNING. So it cannot be a seal blocker.

But BA-04 V4 section 8 stops at the seal and does not look at the coverage rule. Without one of the two options, E6-C4 becomes a de facto BASELINE_READY blocker through BA-02b rather than through the catalog.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-12: the BA-07 V4 reading of the pin state machine and the carry-over of pins and the manifest to a new baseline version
rulings.recommendation:
(1) Pin state machine: agree with BA-07's reading.
- RECORDED is evidenced by the pin-record file alone, with no custody entry of its own.
- PIN_RECORDED is appended only after both ratification records exist, and it cites them.
- An unratified pin is not in custody and cannot be used.

(2) Carry-over: agree with a fail-closed change. Today BA-07 section 8 leaves every pin and manifest usable under v<k+1> unless a later SUPERSEDED or REVOKED entry is appended; that default is fail-open. Instead:
- The ratification records cited by the new BASELINE_APPROVED list each pin-record hash and manifest identity that stays usable. Anything not listed is unusable under v<k+1>.
- A pin may be listed only if its BA-11 section 3.1 slot definition, the scenarios that consume it and its source evidence and tuple are unaffected by the new version. A new build, kind baseline, FPSPEC or source scenario invalidates the matching pins; for EVM_FROZEN, V2.1 27.5 applies.
- 6.2 step 5 checks every IN_USE entry under v<k+1> against that list, or against pins whose baselineVersion is v<k+1>, and reports a violation otherwise.

With this change, BA-07 needs a V5 before its candidate. BA-11 section 3.1 needs no change.
rulings.reasoning:
On (1): AR3-23 says the pin's own seal is the two ratification records 'citados por PIN_RECORDED', so PIN_RECORDED must follow them. AR2-16 requires a custody entry. Tamper-evidence is kept, because the ratifications bind the pin-record hash and the pin is unusable until PIN_RECORDED is anchored before IN_USE (BA-07 section 7).

On (2): AR2-43 ('never a silent change') and AR3-23's baseline-version sequence both require that what stays valid across versions be decided explicitly and verifiably. Under a default-usable rule, a pin frozen under v<k> could feed governing runs of v<k+1> with no auditable decision, and the verifier could not detect it.

2. The characterization build differs from the product build only by the declared harness switches and injection points (AR3-01; BA-04 V4 1.1).
3. Whether an EVM learned or validated across the two builds stays with AQ-V4-01 / CQ-08 (V2.1 27.5).

If the Architect instead wants an explicit new tuple field, that is a V2.6 micro-errata, following the AR3-13 precedent, and it must land before the BA-01 candidate.

Four governing scenarios inject a CANARY_LOAD (variant assembly) inside the governed window:
- NC-E11M-PV and AB-AFTER-MUTATION: 'between PS and PV';
- NC-E11M-PC and U-5: X7, which is before PC and so inside the E-11M window (V2.1 13.2: events from subscription to PC).
Their dry runs (WU-DRY-NC-E11M-PV, WU-DRY-NC-E11M-PC, WU-DRY-AB-AFTER-MUTATION, WU-DRY-U-5) carry the same injection, 'replay its path as a load-path stimulus', and declare E11M 'no assembly-load event inside the governed window ... a load is an E-11M finding (class B) and a design finding'. The canary load is itself such an event, so the criterion of V2.1 13.1 can never be met for these four scenarios. BA-09 section 4's own remedy, preloading the dependent assembly, would preload the canary in the warm-up. The canary would then no longer be a first-time load in the governing runs, and the E-11M negative controls NC-E11M-PV/PC, the U-5 E-11M FAIL (AR3-09) and the AB-AFTER-MUTATION violation (AR3-05) would be neutralized. BA-09 V4 has no text about designed loads: no occurrence of 'canary'.

votes.reasoning:
I checked the finding myself against the worktree at b6fab832 and could not refute it.

1. BA-09 V4 section 4 matches the claim.
   - Line 76 ("Dry-run mode") says each WU-DRY-X runs "the plan, fixture specification, injections and designed stimuli of X". The measured expectation is "no assembly-load event inside the governed window".
   - Line 80 ("Consequences") treats any load in a dry-run window as a design finding. The fix it names is a warm-up revision that adds the path or "preload[s] the dependent assembly".
   - The file never mentions "canary" and gives no rule for loads that a scenario causes on purpose.

2. The BA-04 V4 JSON confirms the four governing sources.
   - NC-E11M-PV (REACH PV) and AB-AFTER-MUTATION (REACH PV) inject CANARY_LOAD (assembly) "between PS and PV".
   - NC-E11M-PC (REACH CP) and U-5 (REACH CP) inject it at X7.
   - All four have target E11M with flag YES. Each expects "E11M: FAIL at PV/PC" and "E10: FAIL" as a collateral; for U-5 this follows AR3-09.
   - All four dry runs exist and carry the same injection: WU-DRY-NC-E11M-PV, WU-DRY-NC-E11M-PC, WU-DRY-AB-AFTER-MUTATION and WU-DRY-U-5, each SEALED_PENDING_PIN_CANDIDATE.
     - Their PLAN_OR_INPUT says "the injections replay its path as a load-path stimulus".
     - Their E11M expectation is "no assembly-load event inside the governed window (WARMUP_COVERAGE_CRITERION, V2.1 13.1); a load is an E-11M finding (class B) and a design finding".
     - E-11M is not in their RECORDED_NOT_ENFORCED list.

3. The window reading holds.
   - V2.1 13.2 records events "from subscription to PC", and 13.1 defines the criterion as no load "inside the governed window" after steps 1 to 5.
   - A canary between PS and PV, or at X7 (between V1 and PC), is therefore inside the window. The criterion cannot be met for these four dry runs as written.
   - NC-E10 (canary at step 5) and NC-WU-FOREIGN (foreign load at step 1, refused at step 3) fall before step 6, so the finding rightly leaves them out.

4. Nothing else in the artifacts handles the case.
   - AR3-02 only says the dry runs "solo miden cargas" in the AR3-01 mode; it says nothing about designed injections.
   - The generic DESIGNED_STIMULUS sentence ("a load-path stimulus of the dry run, not a violation it adjudicates") does not identify or exclude the canary load, and the absolute E11M expectation next to it still counts it.
   - BA-04 V4 section 5.2 takes its expectation from BA-09 section 4.
   - The JSON has no DEFAULTS, AR3_01_MODE or LOG_PROFILES rule excluding designed loads. LP-DRY even says "LOAD_EVENT x1 per assembly-load event (expected zero inside the governed window)".

5. The consequence is real.
   - BA-02b V4 R10 names NC-E11M-PV and NC-E11M-PC as the minimum E-11M negative controls ("a canary load delivers an event").
   - Following line 80's own remedy (preloading the dependent assembly) would load the canary before the window. That would stop the first-time load in the governing runs and so disable these negative controls, U-5's E-11M FAIL (AR3-09) and AB-AFTER-MUTATION's violation (AR3-05).

Severity: MAJOR is right. This is an internal contradiction that makes the per-scenario criterion unmeetable for four governing scenarios, and its remedy is dangerous. It is not BLOCKING because the artifact is an unsealed draft and the fix is textual.

Either fix works: exclude designed injection loads from the measurement by their declared identity, or drop the canary from these dry runs. Both require the four SEALED_AT values to be recomputed.

I checked this myself at worktree commit b6fab832 and could not refute it.

1. Citations are correct. BA-09 V4 line 76 ("Dry-run mode") says each WU-DRY-X runs "the plan, fixture specification, injections and designed stimuli of X", with the measured expectation "no assembly-load event inside the governed window". Line 80 ("Consequences") treats a load in a dry run as a design finding, fixed by revising the warm-up "or else preloading the dependent assembly". A grep finds no occurrence of "canary" in BA-09 V4, and no text excluding designed loads from the measurement.

2. The four governing scenarios load a canary assembly inside the window. I parsed the BA-04 V4 JSON:
- NC-E11M-PV and AB-AFTER-MUTATION inject CANARY_LOAD/assembly "between PS and PV".
- NC-E11M-PC and U-5 inject it at X7, which PLAN_OR_INPUT describes as "between V1 and the PC evaluation".
- All four are GOVERNING with DELIBERATE_VIOLATION_FLAG YES and target E11M. Their expected results are E11M FAIL at PV or PC (U-5 by AR3-09; AB-AFTER-MUTATION by AR3-05).
- The E-11M window of V2.1 13.2 runs "from subscription to PC", so both positions are inside it.
- NC-E10 (module canary at 13.1 step 5) and NC-WU-FOREIGN (step 1) fall before the window. The item correctly leaves them out.

3. The dry runs copy the injection and expect zero loads.
- WU-DRY-NC-E11M-PV, WU-DRY-NC-E11M-PC, WU-DRY-AB-AFTER-MUTATION and WU-DRY-U-5 carry the same CANARY_LOAD injection at the same position.
- Their E11M expectation reads: "no assembly-load event inside the governed window (WARMUP_COVERAGE_CRITERION, V2.1 13.1); a load is an E-11M finding (class B) and a design finding".
- The LP-DRY log profile says "LOAD_EVENT x1 per assembly-load event (expected zero inside the governed window)".
- E-11M is not in the AR3-01 RECORDED_NOT_ENFORCED set, so in the dry run it stays fail-closed (BA-04 V4 section 1.1).
- The canary load is itself a managed assembly-load event inside the window. So the criterion of V2.1 13.1, as these four scenarios state it, can never be met.

4. Existing text does not handle this. The only related wording is the generic DESIGNED_STIMULUS field of every dry run: the injections "are a load-path stimulus of the dry run, not a violation it adjudicates". That field:
- says only that the injection is not adjudicated as a violation;
- does not remove its load event from the zero-load count, which the same scenario's E11M expectation and LP-DRY still require;
- does not stop BA-09's preload remedy.
BA-04 V4 section 5.2 simply defers to BA-09 section 4 ("same ... injections", expectation "no assembly-load event") and adds no exclusion either.

5. The hazard is real. Under BA-09 V4 line 80, a dry-run load leads to preloading the dependent assembly. Preloading the canary during the warm-up would stop it being a first-time load in the governing runs. That would neutralize the E-11M negative controls NC-E11M-PV and NC-E11M-PC, the U-5 E-11M FAIL target (AR3-09) and the AB-AFTER-MUTATION deliberate violation (AR3-05).

6. The governing texts do not resolve it:
- AR3-02 requires dry runs for every governing scenario that enters the window, U-5 by name, and says they "solo miden cargas" (only measure loads).
- AR3-02 and V2.1 13.1 give no exception for designed loads.
- The artifact therefore has to make the reading explicit. The fix the item asks for (exclude load events of assemblies named by a designed injection, identified by declared identity; record them separately as the stimulus; forbid preloading them; realign the four dry-run expectations and recompute SEALED_AT under BA-04 V4 section 1.3) is proportionate and consistent with AR3-02.

Severity: MAJOR stands. A normative, gating criterion cannot be satisfied for four governing scenarios, three of them E-11M negative controls. The artifact's own remedy, applied literally, would defeat those controls.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-06, tuple facet only (two build identities in the tuple; governing scenarios on the characterization build)
rulings.recommendation: DEFER the main question to the BA-04 dimension. The constraint from this dimension's texts: V2.5 section 1 binds CATALOG_FOLDER to 'the build under test', so every run samples the catalog folder that its executing build resolves, including a characterization-build run. V2.5 does not create or settle a second build identity. If the ruling admits governing runs whose tuple carries two build identities, that changes the V2.1 2.1 field set and follows the AR3-13 precedent: a micro-errata. The same errata must say whether CATALOG_FOLDER is sampled once or once per build. V2.5 section 2 line 38 must not be read as deciding this (V25R1-01). Blocks: the BA-04 declarations of AQ-V4-06, which BA-11 V4 line 119 lists as a before-candidate prerequisite of BA-04.
rulings.reasoning: V2.1 section 2 lead and 2.2: a governing run's tuple must equal the baseline tuple in every BUILD_BOUND field, and a mismatch makes the run INVALID. The V2.1 2.1 build rows (repo source SHA of the build, Plugin DLL SHA-256) are single-valued. AR3-01 makes the characterization build's identity a field of its own run's tuple, for non-governing runs only. AR3-13 states that adding a field to the V2.1 2.1 tuple is done by micro-errata.
