findings.claim: BA-02b correctly keeps a NOT_RUNNABLE negative-control cell uncovered, so NEGATIVE_CONTROL_NOT_EVALUATED never becomes MET or PASS there. The scenario expectations that feed the group verdicts do not follow the same rule. First, the two conditional negative controls declare an unconditional 'PASS (designed detection)' contribution, which also holds on their NOT_RUNNABLE branch. Second, the result of the target control on the non-detection branch is stated in two different ways. Third, BA-02b does not say what NEGATIVE_CONTROL_NOT_EVALUATED at acceptance does to V2.1 1.6.
findings.evidence:
- NC-E12C, outcome (line 4503): '... NOT_RUNNABLE for NC-E12C when it does not'. E12C result (line 4505): 'NOT_RUNNABLE for NC-E12C when not delivered'. Group verdict (line 4510), unconditional: 'PASS (designed detection; contributes to the groups served)'.
- NC-S5-O6: its outcome also has a NOT_RUNNABLE branch, but its group verdict (line 8036) is the same unconditional PASS. Its S5 result (line 8032) states only the persisted branch.
- V2.1 1.3 defines PASS as 'the observed outcome and control results equal the scenario-declared expected result'. A NOT_RUNNABLE resolution therefore matches the declared expectation and counts as a 'designed detection' PASS contribution to E12-V and SC-B (NC-E12C), and to AB (NC-S5-O6).
- CER-WIT (line 61): a negative control on its non-detection branch is 'NOT_RUNNABLE for its target'. Yet the 18 WR cells that target E12C (AR3-05) declare E12C 'PASS otherwise' (for example line 11295), while NC-E12C declares 'NOT_RUNNABLE'. That gives two conventions for the same branch.
- BA-02b V4 rule 5 and check 2 say the state at acceptance is NEGATIVE_CONTROL_NOT_EVALUATED, but not what that state does to V2.1 31 check 2, or to V2.1 1.6, whose TRUE requires 'the control-to-group-to-scenario coverage matrix (section 31) is complete'. Check 4, the only incompleteness test (line 267), stays PASS. As written, a control in NEGATIVE_CONTROL_NOT_EVALUATED does not prevent TRUE.

- In BA-04, make the group verdict of every conditional negative control depend on the branch. On the detection branch: PASS as a designed detection. On the NOT_RUNNABLE or non-detection branch: no designed-detection contribution to the groups of the target control, and the cell stays uncovered.
- Use a single convention for the target control's result on that branch, consistent with CER-WIT: either NOT_RUNNABLE for the target, or PASS with an explicit NOT_RUNNABLE coverage flag.
- State NC-S5-O6's S5 result on the non-persisted branch.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-05: cumulative reading of the V2.2 PA-1.4 rows (BA-02b V4 section 3)
rulings.recommendation:
RULING: accept the cumulative reading as the Architect's reading of PA-1.4, recorded like AR3-19, with three precisions.
(1) Cell precedence. Where a PA-1.4 cell contradicts a V2.1 31 cell of the same control, the PA-1.x text governs. The only such cells are the Class cells of LIBRARY_FRESHNESS and CLONE_POLICY_VERIFIED (UNRESOLVED in V2.1), which PA-1.1 and PA-1.2 make B and A. The GROUP column of section 31 is never the group authority: AFFECTED_GROUPS come from PA-1.2 and the groups from PA-1.3.
(2) Union. For SCENARIO CLASSES and MINIMUM CATALOG REQUIREMENT, the clauses of the V2.1 row and of the PA-1.4 row of the same control both apply. The PA-1.4 E-12 row (phase A, determinism, phase C, phase D) applies in addition to V2.1 rows R12 and R13, to all four controls E12A, E12DET, E12C and E12D. 'Subscription' in R13 is phase D (PA-1.2 naming).
(3) S-5 components. The PA-1.4 rows for the S-5 components (P1, P2) are added rows. V2.1 row R03 (S-5, groups AB, PR-REC, PW) also covered what PA-1.1 ratifies as derivations of S-5, so under the same reading it also names S5REC, S5MAN and S5CLO. This changes no state.
No BA-02b V4 state changes under either reading.
rulings.reasoning:
- V2.2 0.2 classifies section 31 as 'amended', not replaced; only 30 and 21.4 are replaced.
- The precedence rule of V2.2 0.1 ('for every clause named in this document, V2.2 governs over V2.1; every other clause of V2.1 stands unchanged') gives V2.2 priority only where the texts conflict.
- PA-1.4 says 'replaced or added rows' but never pairs a row with the V2.1 row it replaces. Its E-12 row spans two V2.1 rows, so any replacement reading would need an invented mapping.
- The union is the fail-closed reading. V2.1 1.6 requires a complete matrix for TRUE, and PA-1.5 repeats this.
- The union imposes no new obligation: every V2.1 clause it keeps is independently required elsewhere in the contract. Examples: warm-up loads outside the manifest refuse the run (V2.1 13.1 row 3, line 718), and validation plans lie structurally outside the learning corpus (V2.1 27.2 step 6 and 27.8, lines 1440-1444).
- A replacement reading would drop only R11 'a warm-up load outside the manifest refuses the run', R12, R13 and R16 'SOURCE_SWAP_CONTROL' as requirements. Every P row that would remain is discharged in BA-02b V4, so no state depends on the choice.
- The ruling does not block candidate readiness beyond fixing the normative text of BA-02b section 3. It is listed among BA-04's before-candidate prerequisites (BA-11 V4 line 119), and BA-02b inherits it through DEPENDS_ON.

rulings.item: R-3: AR3-03 for controls with several conditional negative controls, and the consequence of NEGATIVE_CONTROL_NOT_EVALUATED (BA02V4-N02)
rulings.recommendation:
Rule four points:
(a) The BA-02b rule 5 reading 'NEGATIVE_CONTROL_NOT_EVALUATED unless at least one of its conditional negative controls resolved to its detection branch' is accepted per control. It matches V2.1 31 check 2 ('at least one ... deliberate-violation scenario'), and AR3-03's 'su celda' is per scenario.
(b) At acceptance, NEGATIVE_CONTROL_NOT_EVALUATED makes V2.1 31 check 2 NOT MET for that control.
(c) V2.1 1.6 'the coverage matrix (section 31) is complete' is read as checks 1 to 4 all met. A control in NEGATIVE_CONTROL_NOT_EVALUATED therefore keeps ALT21D_HOST_PASS at NOT_EVALUATED and never TRUE.
(d) The group verdict of a conditional negative control is 'designed detection' only on its detection branch.
rulings.reasoning:
- AR3-03 fixes the BA-02b state ('nunca MET ni PASS') but not what that state does to the predicate.
- As V4 is written, check 4 (the only incompleteness test of V2.1 31) stays PASS, so an E-12 phase C or S-5 negative control that is never evaluated would not prevent TRUE. That defeats the fail-closed purpose of AR2-12, AR3-03 and AR3-04.
- For E12C the choice matters: there are 19 conditional negative controls, and NC-E12C (Wr-A at X6 under CER-WIT) duplicates the stimulus of WR-A-X6.

rulings.item: R-4: contract-assigned membership by scenario class (KS-* to KS and SC-A), related to AQ-V4-03 (BA02V4-N01)
rulings.recommendation: Decide it together with AQ-V4-03: either admit 'a scenario class named by a V2.1 31 row or by V2.1 26.3' as an AR3-06 source (evidence-only, never PASS), or reject it. rulings.item: AQ-V4-01: the RECORDED_NOT_ENFORCED set and build of the governing learning runs EV-L-* and qualification vehicles Q-I14-* (including BA-06 CQ-08)
rulings.recommendation: RULE, split by family. Q-I14-* (4): accept the proposal. They stay GOVERNING qualification scenarios of group Q, on the CHARACTERIZATION_BUILD, with the AR3-01 set recorded only and the vehicle's product outcome not adjudicated. They keep their WU-DRY (AR3-02). Conditions: every other control stays fail-closed, so reach and profile must follow the enforced aborts (BA04V4-06); Wr-OCT and XDATA_WRITE join the writer set; the qualification record binds the characterization build (BA04V4-01). EV-L-* (17): (a) E-12 phases A and C recorded, not enforced: accept (contract-grounded). (b) E-03: reject; enforce it under the pinned LOCK_MODE. (c) E-04: record only for the isolated EV-L-OC-*; enforce it with the pin for EV-L-COMPOSED, a full mirror under R-1. (d) S-1..S-3: NOT_EVALUATED for EV-L-OC-* (REACH LEARN); recorded, not adjudicated, for EV-L-COMPOSED. (e) Build: CHARACTERIZATION_BUILD accepted. (f) Outcome: 'NONE (learning run)', not PROVISIONAL_NON_GOVERNING. CQ-08: using the characterization build for learning is not a tuple change of an EVM validated on the product build, provided the source SHA and the seam code are identical. After the ruling, remove BLOCKED_BY AQ-V4-01 from the 25 scenarios and fix their fields.
rulings.reasoning: Q-I14-*: V2.1 4.3 row I-14 makes the writers 'usable only in characterization builds', and V2.1 10.6 places them in a characterization build. The acceptance in 4.3 (intended effect by an independent read, none when disabled, repeatable) does not depend on any product-control verdict. Q is an EVIDENCE group whose runs must be governing and complete (V2.2 PA-1.3, PA-3), and the product outcome of the vehicle is not an acceptance input. EV-L-*, (a): the EVM does not exist during learning (V2.1 27.1-27.2 steps 2-5; 14.3 levels 2 and 3), and E12-V is evaluable only with a FROZEN EVM (PA-2). (b): V2.1 3.2 keeps E-01..E-13 fail-closed; the LOCK_MODE pin precedes learning (md 2.2 steps 3 and 6), and EV-L-* already carry the slot and LP-LEARN logs LOCK x1, so nothing needs E-03 relaxed. (c): the E04_ADMITTED_SET@R-1 is defined per checkpoint P0/PL/PV/PC of the RackCad command on the designated route (3.3; 2.4). An isolated micro-operation has no such checkpoints, so enforcing that set would refuse by construction. EV-L-COMPOSED is such a command run, and its pin precedes it (step 4). (d): S-1..S-3 are not in 3.2's E-01..E-13 list and are no learning input. (e): isolation (27.2 step 2) needs harness entry points, and harness identity is BUILD_BOUND (2.1 'any payload / observer / harness DLL'). (f): V2.1 26.1 allows 'O1..O7, or none'; PROVISIONAL_NON_GOVERNING_OUTCOME is a 17.2 row 1 concept for invalid or incomplete runs, and 21.1 lists LEARNING runs as non-governing only 'when used as validation'. CQ-08: the governing use of the EVM rests on validation on the product build (27.2 step 6; EV-V-* are PRODUCT_BUILD; PA-2). The learning build identity enters the sealed corpus (27.3 'the sessions that ran them'; 27.6 LEARNING_CORPUS_HASH), and 27.5/14.3 require a new model version only when that identity, the tuple or the seam code changes.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-02: dry-run branches whose source refusal or abort comes from a RECORDED_NOT_ENFORCED control (WU-DRY of NC-E12A, NC-E04-R2, NC-E03-NOT-HELD, NC-E03-REACQUIRE, NC-S1-Y1, NC-S1-Y1-SILENT)
rulings.recommendation: RULE: the dry run takes the declared branch. The characterization build gets a declared dry-run replay switch. When the RNE control records the failure that X's expectation names, the harness forces the same refusal (P0/PL) or abort (PV) at the same checkpoint. The control itself still does not govern, so AR3-02's mode is unchanged. REACH, log profile and events of the six dry runs then equal their sources' (BA04V4-03 closes with only the PLAN and md 5.2/LP-DRY wording). BA-09 V4 section 4 removes these branches from its declared residual. If the Architect prefers the 'not taken' reading, the six dry runs must declare the longer path they run, and md 5.2 must state that the E-11M expectation of the six governing sources rests on no measurement of their own branch.
rulings.reasoning: V2.1 13.1 defines WARMUP_COVERAGE_CRITERION 'for a scenario ... in the non-governing dry runs of that scenario', 'measured, not asserted'. A load inside the governed window of the governing run is an E-11M FAIL (13.1 consequences; 13.2 'any load event in the window is FAIL'), and it would contradict the default E11M PASS of those six negative controls (md 4 UNLISTED_CONTROLS). AR2-42 forbids per-family reduction and borrowing another scenario's dry runs, so the PV abort path that NC-E08-Y* dry runs exercise does not count for NC-S1-Y1. AR3-02 fixes the mode 'solo miden cargas'; a replay switch is a harness stimulus of the dry run and does not make an RNE control govern, so it is compatible. The 13.1 'declared residual' (error and abort paths) concerns what the warm-up cannot exercise. It does not license a dry run to measure a different path from its scenario's.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-03: contribution of the KS-* seam-failure scenarios to group KS
rulings.recommendation: RULE. KS-* serve AB, through S-5 after the caller's abort, and KR, through E-14/E-15 UNDER_CHARACTERIZATION; they carry no PASS-bearing KS contribution. Keep GROUP = AB. Keep KS in CONTRACT_ASSIGNED_GROUPS as evidence only, as a stated extension of AR3-06 to 'a scenario class that the contract lists under a control row it cannot evaluate'. Drop SC-A from their CONTRACT_ASSIGNED_GROUPS. The typed failure (V2.1 15.4) is the scenario's EXPECTED_PROCEDURAL_RESULT and E-14 seam evidence. Then remove BLOCKED_BY AQ-V4-03, which makes the three scenarios SEALED_PENDING_PIN_CANDIDATE.
rulings.reasoning: V2.2 PA-1.4 assigns E-14/E-15 to KR with scenario class KS-*. V2.1 31 row S-5 (AB) requires abort verification 'after MUTATION'. V2.1 15.3 (a POST-WRITE failure obliges the caller to abort) and 17.2 rows 3/4 give O2/O6 by ABORT-VERIFY. V2.1 31 row S-1..S-3 lists KS-* among the classes of the row whose groups are SC-A and KS. Under AR2-08, PASS coverage counts only controls exercised, and a run that aborts at PS reaches none of S-1..S-3 (V2.1 5: staged reads at PV), so the listing is met at design level (31 check 1) and not as PASS evidence. KS's PASS-bearing coverage already comes from S-1/S-2 in CL-CLEAN-* and NC-S1-Y1. SC-A is the scan group ('semantic comparison S-2, S-3 and designed detection at X1..X4', PA-1.3; V2.1 10.6), which the seam classes do not touch. KS is 'Selective seams SL-1, SL-2, SL-4, SL-5, SL-6' (PA-1.3). PA-4 keeps P-8 (seam rollback host evidence) required before the Freeze, and KS-* is the vehicle of that evidence.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-04: whether E6-C4 blocks the catalog seal given AR3-26
rulings.recommendation: RULE: the V4 reading holds. E6-C4 is not a seal blocker of the catalog. NC-S5-O6 stays DRAFT in the sealed bytes (BLOCKED_BY E6-C4 and K-3), with its expectation not declared. Its S-5 negative-control cell is NEGATIVE_CONTROL_NOT_EVALUATED at acceptance. V2.1 31 check 2 for S-5 then stays unmet, and ALT21D_HOST_PASS cannot be TRUE, until a new catalog version declares the scenario from the E6-C4 evidence or a sealed reason records that S-5 cannot be deliberately violated in a governing run.
rulings.reasoning: AR3-26 closes the list of catalog seal blockers: K-3 (to declare the S comparisons), K-8 and the Architect's rulings. E6-C4 is an exploratory host characterization (G-3; V2.1 4.2 E6-C4; V2.1 26.2 EXPLORATORY_NON_GOVERNING), not an Architect ruling. AR3-04 attaches E6-C4 to NC-S5-O6's declaration only. V2.1 26.2: 'a result that no authority determines cannot be declared', and promotion needs a new sealed scenario version. AR3-03: an uncovered negative cell is never MET or PASS. V2.1 31 checks 2 and 4 with 1.6: TRUE is impossible while a mandatory control lacks its deliberate-violation coverage, unless 'cannot be violated by design (recorded with the reason)'. In practice the seal still waits for K-3, which NC-S5-O6 also carries.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-06: governing scenarios on the characterization build, and two build identities in the tuple
rulings.recommendation: RULE: the reading holds, with conditions. (1) The one baseline tuple carries both build identities as BUILD_BOUND fields, and each governing run is bound to exactly one through its TUPLE_REQUIREMENTS. (2) Under CHARACTERIZATION_TUPLE, every build-dependent BUILD_BOUND field is that of the characterization build: Plugin and harness DLL SHA-256, the instrument qualification records for the exact build, and V2.5 CATALOG_FOLDER of the build under test. md 4 must stop saying 'every other field as in FULL_BASELINE_TUPLE' (BA04V4-01). (3) Every instrument used by a governing characterization-build run is qualified on that build, and Q-I14 only there (BA04V4-01, BA04V4-02). (4) The characterization build is built from the identical source SHA, and its switch set and injection points are enumerated in its build receipt (BA-08 K-10), inert unless a scenario names them. (5) Transfer of scan and negative-control results to the product build rests on that construction alone and is disclosed for Owner Act 2. The PARAM-03 sample and EV-V-* validation stay on the PRODUCT_BUILD.
rulings.reasoning: V2.1 10.6 places the I-14 writers 'at a deterministic injection point of a characterization build of the verifier', and 4.3 row I-14 makes them 'usable only in characterization builds'. The scan matrix and the Y-coordinate negative controls that V2.1 31 requires can therefore only run there. V2.1 2 makes a run governing only if 'its tuple equals the baseline tuple in every BUILD_BOUND ... field', and 2.1 already lists 'any payload / observer / harness DLL SHA-256' and 'instrument qualification records for the exact build' as BUILD_BOUND. AR3-01 makes the characterization build identity a tuple field. V2.1 4.3 ('qualified on the exact execution build before any governing run') and 21.1 ('instruments qualified on the exact build'; 'correct binaries') make condition (3) mandatory. V2.5's CATALOG_FOLDER is defined 'of the build under test', which makes condition (2) mechanical. Blocks: the 125 governing characterization-build scenarios and the 21 AQ-V4-01 scenarios.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-14: failure-path event classes (EVM_INCOMPLETE residual) in the 20 governing abort scenarios
rulings.recommendation: RULE: no expectation changes. Record this reading as closed. Phase A is adjudicated over the events delivered inside T_M up to the PV evaluation. On an abort path, the events after the abort decision (Abort(), disposal, and the ABORT-VERIFY read transaction) fall outside phase A: they are logged, not adjudicated (the abort-path counterpart of NG-19b), and never charge E-12. For runs that abort before PV (KS-* at PS), E-12 phase A is NOT_EVALUATED, as declared, and any event the frozen EVM does not explain is recorded as UNEXPLAINED_EVENT evidence for a new EVM version, never as a scenario verdict. PREPARE-W stops (PR-SOURCE-SWAP-NEG-COPY, PW-IMPORT-PARTIAL-FAIL, AB-AFTER-PREPARE-W, NC-CLONE-REPLACE, U-1) are phase 0, log only. The catalog should add the phase tag of post-decision events to LP-PV, LP-PS and LP-PW-STOP. The BA-06 V4 trace-plan residual stays declared.
rulings.reasoning: V2.1 14 fixes phase 0 as log only, phase A as 'unattributable event => fail closed => Abort before Commit()' and phase B as log without adjudication. V2.1 5 records the phase-A verdict in the PV continuity set, and V2.1 8 orders open, writes, staged reads, seal, PV, then Commit() or Abort(). Events after the abort decision cannot 'abort before Commit()' a second time, and V2.1 11 places ABORT-VERIFY in 'a fresh read-only transaction' decided by S-5 (17.2 rows 3/4), not by E-12. V2.2 PA-10 makes EVM_INCOMPLETE 'not a host verdict' requiring a new model version (V2.1 27.5), and V2.1 14.8/27.2 step 4 make unexplained events evidence. The residual therefore does not reach an adjudicated phase of these 20 scenarios, so their declared E12A results (default PASS or CER-WIT conditional) stand.

findings.location: Section 3.3.1 (line 1039); gen.py slot_rule (lines 810-812); mirrored in BA-04 V4 Q-FPSPEC-VECTORS EXPECTED_CONTROL_RESULTS
findings.claim: The instance rule of the slot-unit vectors is not well defined for SV-10 and SV-11. Under its literal reading, SV-10 is always INVALID, so Q-FPSPEC-VECTORS cannot PASS.
findings.evidence: 3.3.1 says the harness 'checks, in exact arithmetic, that the realized difference is <= the slot for an EQUAL vector'. I instantiated SV-10 with the BA-08 V4 section 10 value (1e-9, scratch only): persisted = 6.283185306679586, so |persisted - expected| = 6.28 > TOL. The EQUAL check fails, and the rule then makes the instance INVALID ('never PASS'); BA-04 V4 Q-FPSPEC-VECTORS repeats this. Only the wrapped difference is small: 5.0000029e-10 with exact pi and 5.0000004e-10 with the binary64 NormalizePi of BA-08. Neither value is 'exact arithmetic' on rationals, and the two differ. SV-11's realized quantity is an angle, atan of a binary64 tan(2T), which exact arithmetic cannot evaluate. SV-06 and SV-07 are fine (5.0000004e-10 and 2.0000002e-9).
findings.required_fix: Define the realized quantity per predicate. ABS_DIFF_LE: |p - e| computed exactly on the binary64 values. ANGLE_DIFF_LE: the wrapped difference under the sealed NORM_ANGLE rule, with one stated evaluation method (a certified enclosure with exact pi, or the comparator's binary64 arithmetic). NORMAL_ANGLE_LE: the angle between the normalized realized vectors, from a certified enclosure. An instance whose enclosure straddles the slot is INVALID. Put the same text in the JSON semanticSlotInstanceRule and in the BA-04 V4 Q-FPSPEC-VECTORS text. A NORM_ANGLE rule that does not wrap will then correctly make SV-10 INVALID.

The host decides the order of the DSTYLE pairs, so the row 'sequences whose order the plan determines' does not apply. Two conformant comparators can therefore differ: exact against TOL_LENGTH, and ordered against keyed. If DIMSCALE is read as a scale factor, every unnamed-style dimension comparison waits for K-3. The MTEXT direction vector and integer or boolean fields (Dimtad, Dimdec, flip states) have no row either.
findings.required_fix: Add rows: the override set is compared as a map keyed by DIMVAR group code (order not significant), each value by the class of its variable (list them, including the class of DIMSCALE); integers and booleans are EXACT; direction vectors use a named predicate. findings.location: ENTITY_INSERT blockName and blockDigest (lines 349-350); section 2.4 (line 863); section 5 universe and step 4 (lines 1065, 1072)

rulings.item: AQ-V4-08: whether CONTEXT members are in EXPECTED_AFTER_ABORT, and whether E-08 compares them
rulings.recommendation:
RULE:
(1) ABORT-VERIFY compares every CONTEXT member, both REFERENCE and CONTEXT_VARIABLE, and any difference is O6. The contract fixes this; it is not a kind-baseline option.
(2) The PS re-observation of PREPARE outputs covers the whole record, CONTEXT members included, so an input drift between PR and PS aborts before any write.
(3) E-08 (from the PS baseline to the PV re-observation) compares the REFERENCE members, which accepts BA-08's proposal. It should also compare the CONTEXT_VARIABLE members, unless BA-08 records a reason not to.
BA-05 2.3.5 must be reworded accordingly (BA05V4-N04). Only the E-08 part belongs to the kind baseline.
rulings.reasoning: On (1): V2.1 11 defines EXPECTED_AFTER_ABORT = PRE_COMMAND_STATE_RECORD + EXACT PREPARE_RESIDUE_MANIFEST, 11.2 requires an exact match (else O6), and AR3-11 conditions 2 and 3 place both CONTEXT kinds in that record. On (2): V2.1 5, PS row ('PREPARE outputs equal PP'), and V2.1 7 ('re-observe the relevant elements of the PRE_COMMAND_STATE_RECORD'). On (3): E-08 is the read-set re-observation of V2.1 5 and 11.1 (21.4, row E8), so the contract does not force the context variables into it. But V17 says RACKMIRROR changes no drawing variable, and E-08 is the only in-T_M control before Commit() that would see such a change. Without it, a variable changed inside T_M would surface only as a layer-2 O4 on the attributes that consume it, or not at all. The product writes no context variable at 3375aadb (no Clayer, Cecolor, Celtype, Celtscale, Celweight, Cetransparency or SetSystemVariable writes in src), so including them costs no false FAIL.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-09: plot style name for ST-13
rulings.recommendation:
RULE: FPSPEC-V1 adds no plotStyleName field, and the gap stays declared in the kind baseline, on three conditions:
(a) PSTYLEMODE = 1 is enforced, not only stated. Capture it as a CONTEXT_VARIABLE member of the record, and verify it in every fixture instance's conformance record (BA-08 12.2 and 12.6 currently record only the keys of 11.2). An instance with PSTYLEMODE other than 1 is non-conformant.
(b) The Owner Act 2 disclosure (V2.1 24) states that the CT-21D evidence does not cover named-plot-style (STB) drawings.
(c) Covering STB later needs FPSPEC-V2 and a new baseline (BA-05 2.6).
This ruling changes no BA-05 table, only the 'pending AQ-V4-09' wording in 2.3.5 and 2.4. It does change BA-08 (sections 6, 11.2 and 12).
rulings.reasoning: V2.1 28.1 does not list the plot style among the ENTITY fields ('any type the specification lists'). V17 ST-13 (proposal-v17.md:918) makes PlotStyleName an independent expected value only under STB; under CTB it derives from Color and 'no se asigna una propiedad independiente'. So within CTB fixtures it is not a normative component, and V2.1 11.1's 'component without reader = execution blocker' does not apply. AR3-11 (2) is satisfied by the seven ST-13 fields that ENTITY_INSERT carries. The gap becomes real only on an STB drawing, which condition (a) keeps out of the evidence.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-10: source of dimension overrides
rulings.recommendation:
RULE, layer 1 (BA-05 2.3.2): the stored DSTYLE section of the ACAD extended data, encoded as the lossless RB sequence, is accepted, on these conditions:
(i) the census (section 5, step 5) and the I-12 qualification confirm the storage on the exact build before the candidate, and a different storage changes the table before the seal;
(ii) handle-valued overrides give UNKNOWN, disclosed as an availability cost (EV-83).
Layer 2 (BA-08 section 11 rule 1) is the kind baseline's choice. Recommended: compare the writer-assigned variables through the authoritative reader's typed form (their effective values), keyed by variable, each with its slot class (BA05V4-N07), instead of the stored sequence. If the stored reading is kept at layer 2, compare it as a map keyed by group code, and require qualification evidence that the host stores every assignment, including one equal to the style value.
rulings.reasoning: Layer 1 is exact preserved state (V2.1 28.1). Under V2.1 11.3, any change to a pre-existing homologue must be detected. An override added with the style's value is a stored-state change that an effective-value reading would miss. An effective reading would also fold the DIMSTYLE record, which has its own SYMBOL_RECORD, into every entity digest. The stored reading is the natural extension of AR3-21 (the RB sequence as the reading of 'raw stored bytes'). At layer 2, V2.1 28.2 compares 'the typed form' produced by the authoritative reader against the oracle's expectation. The writer assigns effective properties (LateralHeaderDrawer.cs:362-372), so their effective values do not depend on how the host stores them. The stored form would make the oracle predict host storage details (whether equal values are kept, and the pair order), which sa2 F05-A04 leaves UNCERTAIN.

rulings.item: REJECTED as a third result class (new in V4)
rulings.recommendation: Accept it as a conformance-only class. Add to 2.1 that at runtime a REJECTED is an I-12 defect: the instrument is not RELIABLE, the observation is UNKNOWN (fail closed), and never a digest.
rulings.reasoning: V2.1 28.3 knows only equal, different and UNKNOWN. REJECTED validates producer input in the vectors (RJ-01..RJ-06). The document says a conformant I-12 'never emits such a record' but does not say what a run does if one arises, and V2.1 1.2 and 21.6 require a fail-closed mapping.

rulings.item: Handle-keyed REFERENCE members (BA05V4-N08)
rulings.recommendation: Accept the use of the reference handle as the key of a REFERENCE member, within one session, as the Architect's reading of the V2.1 28.1 ENUMERATION exception. The condition is that BA-05 declares every record and SCOPED_RECORD_COMPARISON containing such members session-bound and excluded from cross-session determinism.
rulings.reasoning: AR3-11 (2) requires each source reference's ST-13 set to be read into the record, so the member needs a key that identifies one reference. A rack GUID does not identify a single reference, because linked copies share it. Every use of the record (PR -> PS -> PV -> ABORT-VERIFY) stays within one session, which is exactly the condition of the contract's ENUMERATION exception.

rulings.item: SCOPED_RECORD_COMPARISON (BA-05 4.1) in place of a full-database fingerprint
rulings.recommendation: Accept.
rulings.reasoning: This is the alternative that the BA05V3-N12 required fix offered. The scope is written before the first observation, the per-member results cover additions and removals through the container ENUMERATIONs, and the coverage limit is repeated in BA-06 V4's declared limit (1).

rulings.item: AQ-V4-11 / CQ-01: the SL-5 'fresh acquire', and the actor of the PREPARE-W checks
rulings.recommendation: RULE yes to both. 'A fresh acquire of the library' (V2.1 15.2 SL-5; 15.8 P-4) names the input SL-5 consumes. Acquiring and opening the private copy are PREPARE-R work of the orchestrator (V2.1 6: 'library input identity and cache freshness (section 19.1)'; 5 row PR; 19.1 step 5 'invalidate explicitly in PREPARE-R before the acquire', step 6 'SL-5 receives the opened Database'; 7.1 'The importer receives that Database'). The PREPARE-W checks (copy re-hash, generation-id revalidation, re-query, fingerprints, effect check, manifest) belong to the orchestrator: outside T_M, under the held lock, with E-06 count 0 before and after each (4.2). SL-5 performs only the clone and returns the structured result.
rulings.reasoning: V2.1 19.1 defines one authoritative source, 'used identically in section 20'. V2.1 7 names no actor for the checks, and ALT-21D V4 3.3 item 1 says 'the product'. The orchestrator owns the lock and T_M (V2.1 8). One consequence: the product-path reads U-03 and U-09 belong to OC-PREP-READ, not OC-IMPORT (BA06V4-N02).

rulings.item: AQ-V4-11 / CQ-02: when the cloning allow-list is checked
rulings.recommendation: RULE as the artifact reads it. The importer carries a fixed declaration of its cloning mode, and it is checked against the allow-list before PREPARE-W starts. Every structured result declares the mode again. A result that declares another mode is the cloning FAIL; a result with no verifiable declaration is UNKNOWN. The allow-list is {DuplicateRecordCloning.Ignore} until a non-replacing equivalent is added by reviewed amendment and qualified by CLONE_NON_REPLACE_CONTROL.
rulings.reasoning: V2.1 7.1: 'PREPARE-W does not start unless the declared mode is on the allow-list', and 'FAIL (differs) or UNKNOWN (cannot verify)'. 'Today DuplicateRecordCloning.Ignore ... or a future equivalent proven non-replacing'. V2.1 4.3.1 and V2.2 PA-12: the acceptance of CLONE_NON_REPLACE_CONTROL includes 'the declared cloning mode is on the allow-list'. A declaration that must exist before PREPARE-W starts cannot come only from a result produced after the first import.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-11 / CQ-03: the outcomes of (i) a pre-import copy re-hash mismatch, (ii) a failed generation-id revalidation, (iii) a post-run copy re-hash mismatch
rulings.recommendation: RULE for (i) and (ii). Before the first completed import, the outcome is O1 under V2.1 17.2 row 2. After at least one completed import, it follows 17.2 rows 3 and 4 (O2 on an ABORT-VERIFY match, otherwise O6), which is 19.1's 'O2 with the residue produced so far'. For (iii), RULE that the acquisition is UNKNOWN (19.1 UNKNOWN row 'the copy hash differs from the record'), recorded as that run's result of the library-freshness control (I-13 / PR-FRESH). The LibraryInputRecord then cannot support a PASS, and the 17.2 product outcome is unchanged. Making it a run status (INVALID) would need an amendment, because the INVALID list of 21.1 is closed.
rulings.reasoning: The copy hash and the generation id are fields of the LibraryInputRecord (19.1 step 3), and library input identity is PREPARE-R content (V2.1 6). A mismatch detected before any product write is therefore an UNKNOWN of a PREPARE-R input, which row 2 covers ('before any product write ... a PREPARE-R FAIL or UNKNOWN'). ALT-21D V4 3.3 item 2 applies the same principle: no product write means O1. Row 3 needs 'a PREPARE-W write'. No current BA-04 V4 expectation changes: PR-SOURCE-SWAP-NEG-COPY injects between imports and expects O2 under row 3.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-11 / CQ-04: a nested transaction inside T_M
rulings.recommendation: RULE NO: a seam may not start a nested transaction inside T_M. Replace the artifact's interim reading ('one observed in the trace creates a new operation class and reopens the review') with this: a nested transaction observed in a seam call is a seam defect against C-131 and C-132 (V2.1 15.3), not a class to learn. Seam implementation review (P-1, P-3) should flag StartTransaction inside the seams. This is a review item and needs no contract change to the closed P-5 list.

ALT-21D V1 row E-06: 'from the start of the single transaction to PV exactly one active transaction, the product's own'. The blind spot between samples (4.2) limits detection. It does not grant permission.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-11 / CQ-05: E-06 sources, logging of the three-valued result, owner of IsTopTransaction
rulings.recommendation: RULE on (a) and (b); (c) is an implementation matter with one constraint. (a) The orchestrator's own bookkeeping is always a source: every transaction it opens, and the count before and after every callee call. It is compared with the counter at every sampling point, and a disagreement makes E-06 UNKNOWN. Events stay optional. (b) The log records YES, NO or UNKNOWN; 'boolean result' is read as 'the result value, never the pointer'. (c) One shared implementation of the typed authority, qualified by E6-C7 and E6-C8 on the exact build, is the reading consistent with V2.1 4.3. Separate implementations would each need their own E6-C7/E6-C8 qualification.
rulings.reasoning: V2.1 4.2 UNKNOWN conditions: 'two sources disagree (counter, own bookkeeping, events)' and 'IsTopTransaction cannot decide' (UNKNOWN must be recordable). V2.1 6: every AUTH-12 call logs the count before and after. E6-C5 qualifies agreement between two sources. V2.1 4.3: every instrument is qualified on the exact build.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-11 / CQ-06: SL-4 and the envelope; 'fresh reread support'
rulings.recommendation: RULE as the artifact reads it. In scope V1, SL-4 writes no envelope. The 15.3 envelope clause binds SL-4 only negatively: it never writes, rewrites or restamps an envelope. For SL-1 and SL-2, 'support' means writing the envelope where RackBlockData.Read and ScanEnvelopes find it (the definition's extension dictionary) and returning the 15.4 handles. For SL-4, it means returning ReferenceId and the handles, so that SL-6 can read and compare SL-R.
rulings.reasoning: V2.1 10.2: 'each sibling's authored envelope (payload)'. 11.1: 'scan of every definition's RackCad payload and envelope'. 25.7: 'one definition and one reference per selected view; envelopes'. 15.4: ReferenceId and the handles of all created objects. BA-05 V4 and BA-08 V4 hold the payload as a member of the definition.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-11 / CQ-07: seam-design details
rulings.recommendation: RULE two points now; DEFER the rest to the seam implementation review (EXEC-3; P-1, P-3, P-6). Nothing in the baseline depends on the deferred points. (1) Host-derived anonymous blocks (*D from RecomputeDimensionBlock, *U from dynamic properties) are not 'created objects' that a seam lists by handle. They enter the phase-A domain through their owning dimension or reference, which is BA-08 V4 section 5's reading and closes BA06V4-N06. Their events are learned as HOST_OBSERVED_STABLE companions of OC-DIM and OC-DYN. (2) A name the sanitizer reduces to empty is detected in PREPARE-R and refused (O1, 17.2 row 2), and a seam that receives one returns InvalidBlockName (PRE-WRITE). Deferred: how 'deterministic result' is verified; whether the returned effective name is compared with the one PREPARE-R expected (V2.1 11.3 supports treating a mismatch as a deviation); the criteria for InvalidPlan and InvalidEnvelope; PRE-WRITE detectability of MissingLibraryBlocks; the semantics of MissingInstances and Diagnostic; and the SL-4 property list, which is BA-08's SL-R and ST-13 plus HOST_DEFAULT_MAP.
rulings.reasoning: V2.1 15.4 lists 'the handles of all created objects' as the seam's result. A seam cannot predict or deterministically return host-generated anonymous records, and BA-05 V4 2.4 excludes anonymous block table records as definitions. V2.1 15.5 says a sanitizer-empty name 'is a failure'. 11.3: names are computed in PREPARE-R under the lock, and 'a collision the policy cannot resolve is a refusal (O1)'. 15.4: InvalidBlockName is PRE-WRITE.

findings.claim:
Step 6 takes the designation only from the anchor records found through the remote tags. It downgrades to NOT_VERIFIABLE when a record says UNDESIGNATED or when no tag exists. A remote rewrite can therefore switch step 6 off even after the copy has been designated.

BA-07's own gates make UNDESIGNATED impossible in a conforming anchor: the designation is required before the seal, and the first anchor comes after every seal.

Step 6 also flags the honest anchoring window as a rewrite.
findings.evidence:
The independent simulation had a designated copy whose holder kept the real anchor list:
- R1: every ct21d-baseline tag deleted, log reset to entries [0,1]. This happens, for example, with a mirror push from a clone that has no ct21d tags. Result: PASS_WITH_DECLARED_LIMITS, status UNANCHORED, step 6 NOT_VERIFIABLE.
- R2: the remote rewritten with re-created tags whose anchor records carry INDEPENDENT_COPY = "UNDESIGNATED", and a forged manifest. Result: PASS_WITH_DECLARED_LIMITS, NOT_VERIFIABLE, although the holder's list differs entirely.

Why a conforming anchor never says UNDESIGNATED:

rulings.item: AQ-V4-12: the reading of the pin state machine and the carry-over of pins and the manifest to a new baseline version (BA-07 V4 5.1 and 8)
rulings.recommendation:
(i) Pin state machine: CONFIRM the draft reading, then remove 'pending AQ-V4-12' from 5.1.
- RECORDED = the content-addressed pin record, with no log entry of its own.
- RATIFIED = both ratification records exist, each citing the pin-record hash.
- PIN_RECORDED (APPROVAL_ROLE) is appended only then and cites both.
- ANCHORED is derived.

(ii) Carry-over: RULE that nothing carries over implicitly. Replace the draft reading with this:
(1) A pin or manifest recorded under v<k> may be used under v<k+1> only if the ruling that approves v<k+1> lists it by hash as carried over. The ruling must state that its slot definition (BA-11 3.1 row and every PIN_SLOT declaration of the sealed catalog) and every tuple field recorded by its source runs are unchanged.
(2) That list is one of the ratification records cited by the v<k+1> BASELINE_APPROVED entry, so the first v<k+1> anchor covers it.
(3) Every item not listed is unusable from BASELINE_APPROVED(v<k+1>) on, and is REVOKED (cause SUPERSEDED_BY_RULING) for the record.
(4) 6.2 step 5 checks (1)-(3). It also checks that a pin record's baselineVersion is the baseline in force at its PIN_RECORDED entry, and that its pinSlot is a sealed slot of that baseline (BA07-V4-02).

If the Architect prefers to DEFER (ii): the deferral does not block the v1 candidate, because carry-over is first exercised at v2 and a later BA-07 version could be sealed with v2. But the deferral record must state that the section 8 carry-over sentence is non-normative and that nothing carries over until a later BA-07 version rules. The candidate bytes should say the same instead of 'this draft's reading'.
rulings.reasoning:
On (i):
- AR3-23 makes the pin's own seal the two ratification records 'citados por PIN_RECORDED'. A log entry can cite only records that already exist, so PIN_RECORDED must follow both ratifications.
- AR2-16 asks for one custody entry in BA-07.
- V2.2 PA-13 is satisfied: approval (PIN_RECORDED) and custody (the ANCHOR_RECORDED that covers it) are separate entries, and the actor of the record is in recordedBy.
- The use precondition already requires PIN_RECORDED to be covered before IN_USE, so nothing a run relies on depends on an unlogged RECORDED state.
- The simulation confirms the machine is workable: RECORDED->RATIFIED->PIN_RECORDED->ANCHORED under one re-anchor, and a missing ratification gives PIN_SEAL_INVALID.

On (ii):
- The contract never carries evidence across instances. V2.1 1.7: a change of the BUILD_BOUND part creates a new instance and 'no evidence transfers'. V2.1 2.1 puts the catalog, FPSPEC, scope, registry and matrix, warm-up definition, kind authority, contract, EVM and 'manifest hash and custody-log reference' in BUILD_BOUND. V2.1 2.2: a mismatch makes the run INVALID. V2.1 29.1: a manifest change is a new capture. V24-N2: a change of the design-time inventory needs a new BA-06 version and a new baseline.
- The draft's 'the ruling decides; excluded items are revoked in the entries that follow' is neither verifiable nor ordered. The simulation's C1 case passes although a governing run consumes an excluded pin under v2.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-13: (a) Q-A1, whether contract-assigned groups enter N_strict; (b) the intent of CHAR_RUNS: (i) its own Owner pair or the derived N_c, and (ii) N_A at the pinned key values or at every key configuration of HDM-CHAR-*
rulings.recommendation:
(a) CONFIRM 'No'. N_strict(s) is computed over GROUPS_SERVED(s) only, and CONTRACT_ASSIGNED_GROUPS never size repetitions. The ruling should say explicitly that 'sirve grupos A o B' in AR3-24 means GROUPS_SERVED, because AR3-06 also uses 'servir' for contract-assigned membership.

(b)(i) CONFIRM the derived N_c: today N_A, and in general the strictest class among the controls that consume the pin or selection. No separate Owner pair. Q-O1 must keep saying that it also fixes CHAR_RUNS; it does now.

(b)(ii) CONFIRM N_A + V(s): N_A runs at the pinned key values carry the intent, plus at least one informative run per varied key. Condition: BA-08 HDM-5 must restrict governing lookups to entries derived from the N_A pinned-key runs, or mark the varied-key entries informative and not eligible for lookup. Otherwise a governing comparison whose key tuple equals a varied configuration would rely on a single-run value outside the intent.
rulings.reasoning:
(a):
- AR3-06: contract-assigned membership 'aporta evidencia y nunca PASS'.
- AR2-08: 'serves' is the GROUPS_SERVED derivation, and PASS coverage counts only CONTROLS_EXERCISED. The AR2-08 fail-closed rule still counts any observed FAIL or UNKNOWN.
- V2.1 1.3 defines PASS over the required governing runs, and V2.1 21.7 attaches the detection intent to the repetitions per group. A contract-assigned run is not a required governing run of that group, so it needs no detection sizing.
- AR2-43 gives evidence groups their own method.
- The other reading changes little (memo E.1: +28 runs at row1, +41 with N_B = N_A+1), so cost does not decide it.

(b)(i):
- V2.1 21.7 'repetitions per group' concerns governing group verdicts. The CHAR runs carry none (AR2-11, AR3-01, AR3-11).
- Their pins are consumed by class-A controls (E4, LK, KS and SC-A are class A in V2.2 PA-1.3). So the explicit statistical intent that 21.7 requires comes from the Owner's class-A pair, which the Owner chooses knowing this effect.
- That keeps the phase-1 reservation of p and alpha to the Owner.

(b)(ii):
- AR3-11 conditions 1, 3 and 4, and BA-08 HDM-4: governing runs on the pinned instances present the pinned key tuple, and the varied runs are informative.
- Condition 4 already makes a missing entry UNKNOWN (O5), so the lookup restriction is sound and costs nothing.
- The other reading adds 756 non-governing runs at row1 (memo E.2, verified: 3 x (10 x 29 - 38)).

findings.location: section 5, domain part (1) (line 128)
findings.claim: A reused SL-Y layer enters the phase-A domain when 'the PRE_COMMAND_STATE_RECORD holds that layer PRESENT, with its handle'.
findings.evidence: BA-05 V4 STATE_MEMBER has the fields memberKey, category, recordKind, expectedName, storedName, state and digest, and no handle. SYMBOL_RECORD_LAYER has no handle. BA-05 V4 2.4 excludes database-local handles except inside ENUMERATION, REFERENCE keys and memberKey. A LAYER member's key is 'READ_SET|LAYER|<name>'. Phase A adjudicates by database handle, class and role (V2.1 14.4), and the event record carries the database handle (V2.1 14.2). The record as specified therefore cannot supply the handle this domain rule depends on.

Either: PREPARE-R resolves each reused SL-Y layer's handle by name, with host symbol-table semantics, under the lock, and logs it (session-local) with the phase-A domain in the PR checkpoint record. Or: add a HANDLE_CLASS ENUMERATION member for the reused layers. Remove 'with its handle' as an attribute of the PRE_COMMAND_STATE_RECORD.

findings.location: BA-08 header PREREQUISITES (lines 22-24); section 16.1, row K-2 and the 'Scenario catalog seal (AR3-26)' paragraph (line 421)
findings.claim: (1) K-2 (the library census) is a BA-08 prerequisite 'before the seal'. (2) 'Of this artifact's items, only K-3, K-8 and the Architect's rulings (K-6) block the seal of the scenario catalog BA-04 V4; K-1 and K-4 do not.'
findings.evidence:
(1) BA-11 V4 section 3.2 lists the census as 'prerequisite of BA-05 (before candidate) and of BA-08 (before candidate)'. The BA-08 header, 16.1 and the BA-11 V4 row for BA-08 say 'before seal'. The same prerequisite of the same entry thus has two gates. Also, BA-05 V4 section 5 requires the census before BA-05's candidate, and BA-08 DEPENDS_ON BA-05. BA-11 V4 section 2 requires every DEPENDS_ON entry to be at least a candidate before a candidate, so K-2 in fact gates BA-08's candidate.
(2) BA-11 V4 section 2 requires, for RATIFIED -> SEALED, 'every entry of its DEPENDS_ON is SEALED'. BA-04 DEPENDS_ON BA-08 and BA-09, and the AR3-25 seal order is BA-08 -> BA-09 -> BA-04. The sentence restates AR3-26 as if K-2 and K-5 did not delay the catalog seal. BA-04 V4 7.4 (C-10, K-5 'not catalog seal blockers') has the same tension.
findings.required_fix:
- Give K-2 one gate in BA-08 and BA-11 V4 (before candidate, which is what the dependency on BA-05 already implies).
- Reword the 16.1 paragraph so that it names the direct (BLOCKED_BY) blockers of the catalog, and add that K-2 and K-5 precede the catalog seal through the BA-11 V4 section 2 gating and the AR3-25 order.
- Alternatively, ask the Architect to state how AR3-26 relates to AR3-25.

findings.location: section 3.2 (line 64); section 8, row W-1 (line 126)
findings.claim: The warm-up plan data are 'the HeaderRunPlan of every view of that fixture's mirrored design, recorded once, offline, as a PLAN_CAPTURE_RECORD (BA-08 V4 section 11.1) from the bound SHA and the bound catalogs', and are due before BA-09's candidate (W-1).
findings.evidence:
(a) The mirrored design D' = mu_Selective(D) cannot be computed at the bound SHA. BA-08 V4 section 3 says 'no RACKMIRROR command', and section 11 rule 4 says 'mu_k is given ... outside CT-21D'. No V4 artifact states D' for any fixture.
(b) PLAN_CAPTURE_RECORD is defined as a per-run record 'taken in PREPARE-R after the effective names and the transform are computed' (BA-08 11.1). Its fields newRackId, effectiveName (which depends on the live block table under the lock, BA-08 section 15), envelopeBytes (which carry NewRackId) and transform have no defined value in data 'recorded once, offline'.
As written, W-1, a before-candidate prerequisite, has no defined source. Producing it would force the implementer either to wait for the mirror implementation (not authorized) or to invent D'.
findings.required_fix:
Define the source of W-1. Either:
(a) the plans that the bound-SHA builders produce for each fixture's authored source design (BA-08 12.2/12.3), with the logical name replaced by a stated non-blank synthetic name, so that the label and SL-Y-added paths run; or
(b) an explicit D' per fixture, derived by the V17 3.6 rule (RUN) and recorded as authored data.
In both cases, declare newRackId, effectiveName, envelopeBytes and transform as synthetic warm-up values, or use a warm-up record type of its own. State that the warm-up plans need only be representative, because the per-scenario WU-DRY runs measure coverage (V2.1 13.1).

rulings.item: AQ-V4-07 (Q-HDM-1): pin source of the unassigned fields of a created SL-Y layer (blocks CL-CLEAN-FXANNBLANK-FP)
rulings.recommendation:
RULE (not defer): record a fourth pin source as an Architect extension of AR3-11 condition (1), in the way AR3-06 extended AR2-08. Add a sealed NON_GOVERNING_BY_DESIGN scenario HDM-CHAR-FXANNBLANK on FX-ANN-BLANK, with the HDM-CHAR properties:
- AR3-01 mode, CHARACTERIZATION_BUILD, GROUPS_SERVED [], pins FIXTURE_INSTANCE@FX-ANN-BLANK and LOCK_MODE;
- it runs after the LOCK_MODE selection and before any governing run that uses S-1..S-3;
- HDM-3 recording and HDM-4 varied settings.
It records, after PC, every SYMBOL_RECORD_LAYER field of the created RACKCAD_ANOTACIONES other than name and colour (linetype, lineweight, isOff, isFrozen, isLocked, isPlottable, transparency), with the key tuple of its own PRE_COMMAND_STATE_RECORD, and also every other in-scope attribute its mirror creates.
Do NOT adopt the proposed form 'also run HDM-CHAR-FXANN on FX-ANN-BLANK': a scenario id binds one fixture slot, and its SEALED_AT covers its expectation fields.
Add to HDM-5: an entry that two HDM-CHAR scenarios supply must agree, otherwise it is UNKNOWN (O5); no choice is made between them.
Consequences:
- CL-CLEAN-FXANNBLANK-FP drops 'K-6 (AQ-V4-07)' from BLOCKED_BY and keeps K-3; HOST_DEFAULT_MAP stays a before-the-first-governing-run pin (AR3-26).
- BA-04 adds the scenario (BA-10 CHAR_RUNS applies).
- BA-11 V4 3.1 adds it to the HOST_DEFAULT_MAP source row.
- BA-08 updates HDM-3, HDM-8, K-4, K-6 and 16.4.
- A created RACKCAD_COTAS has no product-reachable governing scenario; its entries stay absent (UNKNOWN by HDM-5), which is declared.
rulings.reasoning:
- AR3-11(1): the pin may come only from non-governing characterization defined in sealed scenarios. V2.2 PA-9 and AR2-16: it is never derived from governing outputs. That excludes EV-L-OC-LAYER, which is GOVERNING learning on FX-SCRATCH and not a mirror of a product-drawn rack.
- AR3-11(2): the created layer's fields other than Name and Color are set by neither the plan, nor the writer (LayerHelper.cs:25 sets only Name and Color), nor the I-52 authority, so they are in the map's scope.
- AR3-11(4) and HDM-6: they are UNKNOWN until pinned, so without a source the governing SL-Y 'added' scenario that AR3-15 required could never reach EQUAL.
- V17 already places the RACKCAD_ANOTACIONES and RACKCAD_COTAS layer records in the MaterializationContext and CT-50 read set (proposal-v17.md:2198-2206, :3723), so a CT-21D-scoped characterization of them is the L-36 reconciliation AR3-11 asks for (HDM-7), without executing or replacing CT-50.
- None of the three AR3-11 scenarios creates a layer (verified: the FX-1F mirror uses no RackCad layer; FX-ANN and FX-DIM reuse theirs), so an extension of the closed list is needed, and only the Architect can make it.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-04: whether E6-C4 blocks the catalog seal given AR3-26
rulings.recommendation: RULING: E6-C4 is NOT a seal blocker of BA-04, and the V4 reading of section 7.1 holds. The Architect should also record the consequence: with NC-S5-O6 still DRAFT, the sealed catalog does not meet BASE-13, and S-5 has no declared negative control under BA-02b rule 7. E6-C4, or an alternative, therefore stays on the BASELINE_READY path. The alternatives are a non-conditional S-5 negative control, a sealed reason why S-5 cannot be violated, or carrying NC-S5-O6 as EXPLORATORY_NON_GOVERNING with later promotion by a new scenario version (V2.1 26.2). BA-11 BASE-13/BASE-20 should state this. The section 3.3 host-gate plan follows AR3-25 exactly and does not include E6-C4.

E6-C4 is the exploratory host question of AR3-04, not an Architect ruling. V2.1 22 BASE-13 nevertheless requires 'the expected result of every scenario', and BA-02b V4 rule 7 requires a negative control for every mandatory control. NC-S5-O6 is the only negative control of S5 (BA-02b row S5: NEGATIVE CONTROLS '(none)', CONDITIONAL 'NC-S5-O6'). A sealed catalog containing a DRAFT scenario is thus sealable but does not satisfy baseline readiness.

rulings.item: AQ-V4-12: BA-07 pin state machine reading and carry-over to a new baseline version
rulings.recommendation: RULING: ACCEPT the state-machine reading. RECORDED is evidenced by the content-addressed pin record alone. PIN_RECORDED is appended only after both ratification records exist, because it cites them. ANCHORED is derived. ACCEPT the carry-over only with a mechanical default. A pin stays usable under v<k+1> only if (i) its slot exists unchanged in the new BA-11 section 3.1 and the new catalog, (ii) the SEALED_AT of every scenario that consumes it is unchanged, and (iii) the seal hashes of the entries its value derives from are unchanged (BA-08 for FIXTURE_INSTANCE and HOST_DEFAULT_MAP, BA-06 for EVM_FROZEN, BA-01 for the tuple). Otherwise the pin is SUPERSEDED or REVOKED (SUPERSEDED_BY_RULING). The approving ruling lists the carried pin-record hashes in the BASELINE_APPROVED ratification records. Because pin records are never edited and keep baselineVersion = v<k>, the IN_USE check accepts a carried pin through that list, not by equality of baselineVersion. BA-11 bytes need no change.
rulings.reasoning: AR3-23 fixes 'RECORDED -> RATIFIED -> ANCHORED' and says 'el sello propio del pin son los registros de ratificación ... citados por PIN_RECORDED', which is the order BA-07 5.1 adopts. BA-07 section 8 (line 303) leaves carry-over to a free ruling. It gives no criterion and no representation, while the pin record's baselineVersion (5.1 line 143) is immutable. Without a default, a baseline re-version could silently keep a pin whose source or consuming expectation changed. V2.1 26.2 says an evidence-derived expectation 'is pinned to that value's version'.
